name: Buy-then-build HVAC company packaged for a PE add-on exit
thesis: Buy a retiring owner's HVAC shop at 2-3.5x owner earnings (typical small shop sells ~$800K per BizBuySell data; https://dealprospectors.com/hvac-business-sale-multiples/ ; median owner earnings $232,307 on $1.04M sales, https://www.bizbuysell.com/learning-center/valuation-benchmarks/hvac/), drive maintenance-agreement penetration past 40% of revenue (the primary lever that unlocks 7-10x EBITDA in competitive processes vs. 3.0x low / 5.5-7.0x mid; https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/), and sell to a PE add-on buyer paying 4-8x EBITDA at the sub-$2M tier and 6-11x at $2M+ (https://pipelineon.com/blog/private-equity-buying-hvac/) — the multiple arbitrage on a shop grown to $1M EBITDA is $3-6M of equity from a ~$50K cash injection. Capital: SBA 7(a) requires a 10% injection, up to half of which can be a full-standby seller note (https://www.clearlyacquired.com/blog/sba-7a-seller-notes-standby-rules), so ~$40-50K cash covers an $800K-1M deal.
who_pays: Homeowners and light-commercial property owners for repairs, replacements and maintenance plans; a private-equity platform pays the exit.
why_now: 110,000-technician shortage with five retiring for every two entering (https://hirealigned.com/learn/hvac-technician-shortage-statistics) gives pricing power; PE firms and platforms were ~51% of tracked HVAC M&A through June 2025 and Apex alone did ~60 add-ons in 2025 (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/private-equity-hvac-2026/); Blackstone paid ~$2.5B / ~18.5x EBITDA for Champions Group on Feb 17, 2026 (same source, citing Bloomberg), so platforms are hungry for add-ons; 2.3-3 million boomer-owned businesses will transition over the next decade with ~50% lacking a succession plan, and 80%+ of SBA 7(a) loans are under $500K (https://www.acquisitionace.io/data/statistics). Fit: Joshua already runs the call center/dispatch/lead-gen stack an HVAC shop lives on.

name: Recurring-route pest control company built to 80%+ contract revenue (PE-exit spec)
thesis: Launch for $15-65K all-in, break even in 6-14 months, and take home $80-140K by year two as a solo operator in a 200K+ metro (https://oncallclerk.com/blog/how-to-start-a-pest-control-business); 150 quarterly accounts at $80-120/visit is $480-720 per customer per year at 20-40% net margins (same source); then stack routes to $1M+ EBITDA, where 85%-recurring, sub-1.5%-monthly-churn books command 6.5-8x EBITDA and the recurring mix alone is worth a $2M valuation swing on a $1M-EBITDA business (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/pest-control-business-valuation/).
who_pays: Homeowners on quarterly plans; restaurants, property managers, and RV parks/campgrounds on monthly commercial contracts.
why_now: $29.7B US market with 34,000+ operators and PE at ~60% of all pest M&A, with Anticimex, Arrow and Massey still aggressively acquisitive (https://www.breakwaterma.com/blog/pest-control-company-valuation-multiples-2026); pest control carries a 3.3x low / 5-6x mid / 8x+ high EBITDA band, top of the home-services stack (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/). Fit: route density is a lead-gen and dialer problem — Joshua's day job — and his RV-resort employer is a ready-made commercial anchor account.

name: Texas data-center electrician → industrial electrical contractor (with a Generac-dealer home lane)
thesis: Get paid from day one as an apprentice (Texas average $44,206/yr, https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Salaries/Apprentice-Electricians-Salary--in-Texas ; $57-59K in Houston/Austin, https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/houston-tx-apprentice-electrician-salary-SRCH_IL.0,10_IM394_KO11,33.htm) on data-center builds where the Abilene Stargate site pays electricians double what local subs can (https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/28/data-centers-texas-electricians-builders/) and journeymen/foremen in hot regions hit $130/hr before overtime (https://www.rinvio.com/blog/electrician-shortage-data-center-boom); then flip to contractor, where electrical companies trade 3.2x low / 5-6.5x mid / 8x high EBITDA (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/) and each whole-home standby generator install bills $8,500-13,000 (https://ohmselectricnv.com/electrical-services/generac-standby-generator-installation-costs-in-2026/). Honest constraint: a Texas journeyman license needs 8,000 OJT hours (~4 years) (https://www.buildforce.com/resource/how-to-become-a-licensed-journeyman-electrician-in-texas), so the contractor step needs a master-licensed partner in year 2-3.
who_pays: Data-center general contractors and electrical subs (wages, per diem, bonuses); later homeowners and businesses buying generators, EV chargers and service upgrades; commercial/industrial owners.
why_now: Texas is on track to pass Northern Virginia as the world's largest data-center market — 300+ operating, ~100 planned (https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/28/data-centers-texas-electricians-builders/); the US needs 300,000+ more electricians while ~20,000 retire yearly and electrical is 45-70% of data-center construction cost, making electricians the binding constraint on AI buildout (https://www.buildforce.com/resource/the-electrician-shortage-in-2026 ; https://www.rinvio.com/blog/electrician-shortage-data-center-boom); Texas grid strain pushed standby-generator demand to record levels (https://pipelineon.com/blog/electrician-generator-install/).

name: Rural septic pumping + mandated aerobic maintenance-contract route (Ark-La-Tex)
thesis: A used vacuum truck runs $40-120K (https://www.septictrucks.com/how-much-does-a-septic-truck-cost-in-2026-real-prices-and-buyer-guide/), each residential pump-out bills $300-600, and owner-operators run 50-65% gross / 20-35% net margins (https://www.septictankhub.com/blog/is-septic-business-profitable/) — one truck grosses $75-300K, 2-5 trucks $500K-2M+ (https://servicecore.com/blog/owning-a-septic-pumping-business-salary/). The recurring kicker: Texas requires every aerobic system to carry a $200-500/yr maintenance contract with inspections every 4 months by a TCEQ-licensed provider, backed by fines up to $100/day (https://www.texassepticguide.com/learn/aerobic-septic-maintenance-texas) — a legally mandated subscription book.
who_pays: Rural and exurban homeowners (mandatory contracts, pump-outs, repairs), RV parks and campgrounds, home sellers needing inspections, builders needing new installs.
why_now: Texas has ~2.6 million septic systems and demand is growing faster than almost anywhere in the country as housing pushes into rural counties (https://septicandwell.com/articles/septic-system-texas); the TCEQ Installer I license needs only a $460 TEEX course, a $111 fee and an exam with no prior experience, and Installer II (aerobic systems) follows after one year (https://www.servicetitan.com/licensing/septic/texas); the trade is described as low-competition, high-profit (https://www.ownedandoperated.com/post/how-to-start-a-septic-business). Fit: an RV-resort membership company is a built-in commercial septic customer.

name: Direct-cremation storefront with online arrangement (contracted crematory, no retort)
thesis: Cremation hit 63.4% nationally in 2025 and is projected past 70% by 2030 (https://us-funerals.com/2026-us-cremation-rate/); direct cremation at $1,000-3,000 is the fastest-growing category in the industry (https://www.localcremationguide.com/blog/cremation-industry-trends-2026); a storefront that contracts a third-party crematory skips the $485K lean-crematory build (https://financialmodelslab.com/blogs/startup-costs/crematorium) and runs on a removal van, a leased arrangement office, and a web funnel. Capital estimate: $75-150K (basis: lean crematory cost stack at https://planpros.ai/articles/cremation-business-startup-cost/ minus the $150-350K retort and install). Texas licensing: a TFSC funeral-establishment license plus a licensed funeral director on staff (https://tfsc.texas.gov/establishmentlicensing); Texas law does not require a funeral director to deal with a crematory, though most crematories require one (https://www.acremation.com/state-regulations/).
who_pays: Families of the deceased (paid at arrangement, increasingly online and pre-need); hospice and nursing-home referral flow.
why_now: Only ~36% of funeral homes offer online cremation arrangement, with 25% more planning to within four years (https://www.cremation.green/dissecting-the-nfda-2025-cremation-burial-report-stats/); at 80% cremation, a typical traditional funeral home's revenue drops toward ~$300K, so incumbents with embalming rooms and chapels cannot match a lean direct-cremation price (https://us-funerals.com/2026-us-cremation-rate/). Fit: the entire product is a web funnel plus a phone/arrangement process — Joshua's exact skill set.

name: IUEC elevator mechanic via the NEIEP apprenticeship
thesis: Elevator mechanics have the only six-figure BLS median among trades ($106,580; San Jose metro median $169,560) (https://tradecolleges.org/blog/trade-programs/elevator-installer-repairer-careers); IUEC Local 80's 2026 mechanic rate is $53.40/hr with probationary apprentices at $26.70 and year-2 at $34.71 (https://unionpayscales.com/trades/iuec-elevator-installers/); raises are written into the collective bargaining agreement, tied to time served (https://www.neiep.org/iuec-apprenticeship-faq/how-much-does-being-an-iuec-apprentice-mechanic-pay/).
who_pays: Otis, Schindler, TK Elevator, Kone and independent elevator contractors under IUEC contracts; ultimately building owners under mandated inspection, maintenance and modernization.
why_now: ~2,000 openings per year through 2034 with 5% growth and a large cohort nearing retirement (https://tradecolleges.org/blog/trade-programs/elevator-installer-repairer-careers); labor shortages are making qualified elevator crews a critical-path item on construction schedules (https://www.fieldboss.com/blog/its-a-good-time-to-be-an-elevator-mechanic/). Reachable: paid from month one; 4-5 years to full mechanic rate (https://www.neiep.org/iuec-apprenticeship-faq/).

name: Fire-protection ITM + backflow compliance route (NFPA 25/72 mandated recurring revenue)
thesis: Annual fire-sprinkler inspection/testing tickets run $500-5,000 at 50%+ gross margin, backflow tests bill $75-150 per device in under 30 minutes, and one property manager with 40 buildings at $750 is $30K of annual recurring revenue from a single relationship (https://www.withessential.com/resources/grow-fire-protection-business); municipalities require backflow assemblies tested every 12 months, creating built-in recurring demand (https://bizbite.io/businesses/backflow-testing); companies with 60%+ recurring inspection/monitoring revenue trade at 4-5x SDE (https://ctacquisitions.com/fire-sprinkler-business-valuation-and-buyer-demand/). Capital estimate: $20-40K for a van, test kits, software and licensing (basis: ASSE certification runs $500-1,000 per https://www.withessential.com/resources/grow-fire-protection-business).
who_pays: Commercial property owners, property managers, HOAs, hospitals, schools, restaurants and municipalities — under legal mandate enforced by fire marshals, water utilities and insurers.
why_now: Demand is written into code (NFPA 25 and 72), so revenue is mandated rather than marketed, which is exactly why investors are chasing the category (https://www.withessential.com/resources/grow-fire-protection-business). Texas licensing: TCEQ BPAT needs a 40-hour course, two years of water-related experience and an exam (https://www.tceq.texas.gov/licensing/licenses/bpatlic); sprinkler ITM requires a TDI RME-Inspector or RME-General (https://tdi.texas.gov/rules/2007/0303-059.html) — so the 24-month path is to partner with or hire a licensed RME/BPAT while Joshua builds the account book and scheduling system.

name: Roll-off dumpster rental fleet with online self-booking (Ark-La-Tex contractors and storm cleanup)
thesis: One truck with a driver reaches $350-450K annual revenue at 30-40% gross margin after tipping fees (https://www.curbwaste.com/dumpster-rental-business-profitability), $120-250K owner earnings per truck (https://financialmodelslab.com/blogs/how-much-makes/dumpster-rental-service), $250-350 net profit per haul (https://quipli.com/resources/how-profitable-is-a-dumpster-rental-business/), and a ~$90K startup typically pays off in 18-24 months (https://www.dumpsterrentalsystems.com/blog/how-to-start-dumpster-rental-business/) — equipment financing brings cash-in near the $50K mark.
who_pays: Roofers and remodel contractors (repeat weekly accounts), homeowners doing cleanouts, storm-restoration crews, property managers and municipalities.
why_now: Texas averages $4B+ in annual wind/hail claims and DFW/North Texas see 5-8 significant hail events a year (https://dgagency.co/blog/texas-roofers-storm-restoration-playbook-2026) — every reroof and storm cleanup needs a bin; small metros are underserved by national haulers. Fit: online booking, dispatch and route software is the product Joshua already builds.

name: Mobile diesel fleet-maintenance contractor on the I-30 freight corridor (Texarkana)
thesis: Diesel labor bills ~$190/hr (https://www.fullbay.com/blog/diesel-repair-shop-profit/), mobile operators in high-demand corridors bill $125-200/hr and experienced operators clear $150K+ (https://heavydutyjournal.com/how-to-start-a-mobile-diesel-repair-business-2025-guide/), a 3-5 tech operation does $300-500K+ (https://www.pro.trackara.app/blog/mobile-mechanic-salary), and launch cost is $50-100K versus $200-500K for a brick-and-mortar shop (https://heavydutyjournal.com/how-to-start-a-mobile-diesel-repair-business-2025-guide/). Hybrid structure: hire one certified diesel tech; Joshua runs contracts, dispatch and preventive-maintenance scheduling software.
who_pays: Small trucking fleets, owner-operators, distribution centers, ag and construction equipment owners — on retainer PM contracts plus premium emergency roadside call-outs.
why_now: 60,000-70,000 open diesel technician positions on Indeed alone, 65% of repair shops understaffed, and $2.4B/yr lost to deferred repairs (https://fleetrabbit.com/blogs/post/diesel-technician-shortage-fleet-maintenance-crisis-2026); Texarkana sits on I-30 between Dallas and Memphis with ~77,040 vehicles per day through the city (https://www.texarkanatexas.gov/m/newsflash/home/detail/385) and corridor freight traffic projected to nearly double by 2040 (https://ftp.txdot.gov/pub/txdot-info/i30/flier-truckers.pdf).

name: Storm-restoration roofing company in Texas hail alley (supplement-driven, locally rooted)
thesis: Texas has no state roofing license (https://www.getjobber.com/academy/roofing-license/texas/), most new roofing companies launch on $50-80K with owner-operators as low as $30K (https://www.howmuchtostart.com/roofing-company ; https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/how-to-start-roofing-company/), residential storm claims average $9,000-15,000 (https://www.subcontractorhub.com/blog/roofing-insurance-claim-process), insurance restoration runs 15-25% margin and repairs 25-40% (https://build-folio.com/contractor-guides/roofing-profit-margins/), and disciplined supplementing recovers the 20-40% of revenue an uncontested estimate leaves on the table (https://www.subcontractorhub.com/blog/roofing-insurance-claim-process). Roofing companies exit at 2.5x low / 4-5.5x mid / 7x high EBITDA (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/).
who_pays: Insurance carriers via homeowner claims; homeowners on retail replacements and repairs; commercial property owners.
why_now: Texas averages $4B+ in annual wind/hail claims and DFW/North Texas see 5-8 significant hail events per year (https://dgagency.co/blog/texas-roofers-storm-restoration-playbook-2026); 75% of roofing/exterior contractors expect revenue growth in 2026 (https://calljolt.com/blog/roofing/roofing-industry-statistics-2026); carriers retreating from hail markets are squeezing out out-of-state storm-chasers (https://www.lovelandinnovations.com/uncategorized/the-end-of-storm-chasing-what-roofing-contractors-need-to-know/), leaving the market to local operators with real sales systems — canvassing, dialers, show rates and reps are Joshua's day job. Cost note: Texas roofing workers' comp runs $15-25 per $100 of payroll (https://insuranceproagencies.com/insurance/compare/best-roofing-insurance-texas).

name: 6G-certified pipeline / LNG welder (Gulf Coast and Local 798 travel work)
thesis: Pipeline welders earn $50-125K, and 6G-combo welders who travel earn $80-150K+ with overtime; Pipeliners Local 798's 2025-26 scale is $52.07-53.00/hr journeyman plus $165/day per diem (https://www.westernweldingacademy.com/blog/what-is-the-average-pipeline-welder-salary-in-the-united-states-in-2026); Houston is the largest industrial welding market in the US and Gulf Coast LNG, petrochemical and refinery work keeps certified pipe welders busy year-round (https://skillit.com/blog/what-welders-make-across-us).
who_pays: Pipeline contractors, LNG and petrochemical EPCs, refineries and fabrication shops — often union scale plus per diem.
why_now: 82,500 welders are needed per year, the Permian Basin and Gulf Coast are in acute shortage, and contractors have raised skilled wages as much as 20% in three years (https://www.westernweldingacademy.com/blog/why-is-the-welder-shortage-getting-worse-in-2026); rising labor costs are now the constraint threatening new US LNG projects (https://www.naturalgasworld.com/increasing-us-labor-costs-threaten-to-derail-new-lng-projects-111808). Reachable: a 6-9 month welding program plus a 6G test puts a motivated adult on payroll inside 12 months; Texarkana is a few hours from the Gulf Coast hubs.

name: Utility lineman via apprenticeship, stacking storm-restoration double time
thesis: Lineman median pay is $92,500 (~$46.25/hr), rising to $102,550 in electric power generation/transmission/distribution (https://wealthvieu.com/how-much-do-linemen-make/); apprentices start $25-35/hr and journeymen earn $40-55+/hr (https://skilledtradespath.com/lineman-salary/); a journeyman on a storm call working 16-hour double-time shifts for 7 days grosses $11,200 before per diem, and storm work adds $20-60K+ per year for those willing to travel (https://www.powerlinemanjobs.com/storm-pay-for-linemen-how-much-linemen-make-chasing-storms).
who_pays: Investor-owned utilities, electric co-ops and line contractors (Quanta, MasTec, Pike) — funded by rate-based grid capex and FEMA-backed storm restoration.
why_now: US electricity demand is rising ~3% annually on EVs and data centers, 103,000 miles of new transmission are projected within 13 years, and more linemen are retiring than entering, driving wage hikes and overtime (https://www.linemancentral.com/statistics ; https://www.linemancentral.com/post/lineman-jobs-are-in-high-demand); nearly 30% of union electrical workers are at or near retirement (https://ablemkr.com/the-state-of-skilled-electrical-labor-2026/). Reachable: a ~15-week line school followed by a paid apprenticeship — earning from month one, with hurricane-season storm checks in year one.

name: Hyperscale data-center electrician (travel crew) -> licensed electrical subcontractor
thesis: Electrical work is 45-70% of data-center construction cost and Microsoft's president calls the electrician shortage the single biggest obstacle to its US buildout, so a helper-to-journeyman who chases hyperscale sites clears $150K+ with overtime and per diem and then flips into a subcontracting crew that GCs pay platform-level rates (https://www.rinvio.com/blog/electrician-shortage-data-center-boom, https://thebirmgroup.com/data-center-electrician-150k-salary/).
who_pays: Electrical contractors and GCs on hyperscale builds (Stargate/Oracle, Microsoft, DataBank) funded by hyperscaler capex; later, the same GCs and utilities pay your crew as a subcontractor.
why_now: Data-center electricians quoted $89K-$121K base plus OT, with per diem of $100-$150/day adding $30-40K on a 10-month assignment (https://thebirmgroup.com/data-center-electrician-150k-salary/, https://buildermuse.com/labor-wages/data-center-construction-wages-2026-by-trade/); Texas data-center journeymen $38-46/hr straight time, $50+ at better contractors, NoVA $72-75/hr all-in (https://buildermuse.com/labor-wages/data-center-construction-wages-2026-by-trade/); AI data centers may need 300,000+ additional electricians this decade and Microsoft is flying electricians in from 75+ miles away (https://www.rinvio.com/blog/electrician-shortage-data-center-boom, https://www.buildforce.com/resource/the-electrician-shortage-in-2026); $88B of US data-center starts tracked for the next six months and 248 projects planned in Texas (https://news.constructconnect.com/data-centers-could-be-a-bright-star-in-texas-construction-for-2026-and-beyond, https://www.texastribune.org/2026/06/26/texas-data-center-guide-what-you-need-to-know/); Texarkana itself now has the $3.5B, 500-acre Project Big Pine and a 200 MW Miller County campus (https://www.texarkanagazette.com/news/2026/apr/28/texamericas-centers-project-big-pine-sets-table/, https://www.thefan1079.com/news/local-news/200-megawatt-ai-data-center-planned-north-of-texarkana/). Reach caveat: apprentice/helper pay plus OT and per diem is what is reachable inside 24 months; the journeyman license itself typically takes ~4 years (not separately sourced here). Fit for Joshua: low-medium (career change), but the crew-business layer uses his ops/staffing skills.

name: Workforce-housing RV park / crew-lodging operator next to AI megaprojects
thesis: Hyperscale builds drop 1,500-6,000 traveling tradesmen into towns with no beds and each carries ~$110/night of GSA-benchmark lodging per diem, so full-hookup pads and crew lodging within 30 minutes of a site rent at near-full occupancy for the 2-4 year build and then convert to snowbird/long-term inventory.
who_pays: Traveling electricians, pipefitters and their contractors (per diem), GCs and staffing firms that block-book sites, then snowbirds and long-term residents once the cranes leave.
why_now: Stargate brought ~6,000 workers to Abilene (pop. ~100K) and average rent hit ~$2,600, up nearly 50% in a year (https://texasstandard.org/stories/stargate-data-center-abilene-housing-crisis-rising-rents-homelessness-shortage/, https://ktxs.com/news/local/thousands-of-ai-data-center-workers-drive-up-abilene-rents-amid-scarce-housing); monthly RV sites there run $500-$800 (https://inezspring.com/stargate-data-center-worker-housing/, https://www.bigcountryhomepage.com/news/data-center-growth-strains-abilene-housing-as-rv-park-proposal-draws-scrutiny/) and Taylor County approved a 2,313-site RV park aimed squarely at data-center crews (https://nstarba.com/new-2313-site-rv-park-what-it-is-why-its-coming-and-what-it-means-for-texas/); FY2026 GSA per diem is $110 lodging + $68 M&IE, and rural markets like Abilene and Lancaster PA have almost no lodging inventory (https://globeo.com/ai-data-center-crew-lodging/); DataBank's Red Oak campus alone expected 4,000-5,000 workers (https://www.bomaproperties.co/post/data-center-workforce-housing-boom); Texarkana's $3.5B Project Big Pine and the 200 MW Miller County campus are next in line (https://txktoday.com/news/project-big-pine-400-acre-data-center-campus-planned-for-texarkana-region/, https://www.texarkanagazette.com/news/2026/aug/15/public-records-reveal-site-of-planned-ai-data/). Capital: a ground-up park exceeds $50K; no sourced per-pad development cost was found, so the low-capital entry is master-leasing or managing an existing park, or leasing land for a 20-50 pad crew lot (estimate, unsourced). Fit for Joshua: very high, he runs marketing/ops for an RV-resort membership company.

name: AI voice receptionist + missed-call recovery agency for home-service contractors
thesis: Contractors miss 60-80% of inbound calls worth $200-$2,000 each, and a white-labeled voice agent that answers, books and texts back costs pennies per minute but sells at $300+/month, producing 70-90% gross margins on recurring revenue that no receptionist can match.
who_pays: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, pest and dental/med-spa owners on $49-$325/month plans plus per-minute overage; upsell to $1-5K/month workflow-automation retainers.
why_now: Home-service firms miss ~58% of calls and lose ~$26B/yr, with 60-80% miss rates common and $200-$2,000 per missed call (https://calljolt.com/blog/guides/home-service-business-missed-call-statistics, https://calljolt.com/blog/hvac/home-service-industry-phone-statistics); retail AI-receptionist plans run $49-$325/month with $0.65-$2.25/min overage (https://www.aicontio.com/2026/04/20/the-complete-ai-voice-buying-guide-for-2026-platforms-vendors-use-cases/); wholesale minutes from $0.09 resold at $0.25-$0.60 (https://www.leadlock.ai/blog/best-white-label-ai-voice-agent-platforms-for-agencies/, https://www.centricallai.com/article-and-insight/white-label-ai-voice-agents); agencies report $10K-$100K+/month recurring at 70-90% margins with 60-90 day payback (https://voiceaiwrapper.com/insights/ai-voice-technology-agencies-revenue-growth-2026); 73% of contractors switching see positive ROI within 30 days (https://calljolt.com/blog/hvac/home-service-industry-phone-statistics); automation retainers of $1-5K/month stack on top, one operator showing 12 clients = $36K/month (https://automatonagency.com/insights/ai-automation-agency-economics, https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/start-ai-automation-business-case-studies). Fit for Joshua: extremely high, he runs dialers/show-rate ops by day and ships apps solo by night.

name: GEO/AEO agency: get brands cited by ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews
thesis: The click era is ending and CMOs are moving budget to being the answer inside AI engines, a service line that barely existed in 2023 and now commands SEO-agency-level retainers with a fraction of the competition.
who_pays: Mid-market and DTC brands, franchises, law/medical/home-service groups and their CMOs; white-label to legacy SEO agencies that cannot deliver it.
why_now: 94% of CMOs plan to increase AEO/GEO investment in 2026 per Conductor's State of AEO/GEO report (https://minuttia.com/best-geo-agencies/); GEO services market projected $1.25B (2026) to $13B (2033) (https://www.rswebsols.com/news/generative-engine-optimization-geo-services-market-projected-to-reach-usd/); alternate estimate $848M (2025) to $19.8B (2034) at 50.5% CAGR (https://marketintelo.com/report/generative-engine-optimization-geo-market); GEO statistics framed as 'the end of the click era' (https://digitalagencynetwork.com/generative-engine-optimization-statistics/); full 2026 playbook exists to execute against (https://searchengineland.com/mastering-generative-engine-optimization-in-2026-full-guide-469142). Fit for Joshua: high, marketing background plus ability to build citation-tracking tooling himself.

name: Forward-deployed AI engineer (FDE) at an AI lab, fintech or consultancy
thesis: Companies pay $200K-$630K total comp to someone who can sit inside a customer and make AI agents actually work in production, and the role is being filled by builders with shipped products rather than credentials.
who_pays: AI labs, Palantir-style platforms, big banks/retailers and consultancies (BCG X etc.) hiring FDEs out of enterprise AI budgets.
why_now: FDE total comp ranges $200K-$630K+ (https://www.recruitingfromscratch.com/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-salary-in-2026-full-guide); frontier labs $300-450K mid-level and $500K+ senior, Fortune 500 $190-420K, Palantir $215K median (https://getperspective.ai/blog/2026-forward-deployed-engineering-compensation-report-1200-fdes); BCG hiring FDEs from campus at $110-190K (https://managementconsulted.com/bcg-forward-deployed-ai-engineer/); reports of an ~800% spike in FDE listings (https://www.gsdcouncil.org/blogs/forward-deployed-engineer-high-paying-ai-career-guide); ~982 open roles tracked (https://joinplank.com/fde-job-market). Fit for Joshua: high on profile (shipped apps + ops/CRM/dialer domain is the FDE archetype); caveat that many roles are travel-heavy or hub-city based.

name: Prediction-market liquidity provider + edge-tooling builder (Kalshi/Polymarket)
thesis: Prediction markets went from under $5B to ~$50B monthly volume in ten months and the exchanges are paying cash rewards for resting liquidity, so a disciplined market-making book plus sellable data/terminal tools earns spreads, subsidies and subscriptions on a market that did not exist at scale in 2023.
who_pays: Kalshi's Liquidity Incentive Program (up to $1,000/market/day open tier, $50K/series/week for designated market makers), counterparties who cross your spread, and traders subscribing to your analytics/API.
why_now: Combined Kalshi+Polymarket monthly volume rose from under $5B in Sept 2025 to over $50B in July 2026 and $45.3B in August (https://defirate.com/prediction-markets/volume/, https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/05/27/trading-volume-on-prediction-markets-has-soared-in-recent-months/); Kalshi's LIP pays $1-$1,000 per market per day through Jan 1 2027, MM tier caps $50K/series/week (https://help.kalshi.com/en/articles/13823851-liquidity-incentive-program, https://www.cftc.gov/sites/default/files/filings/orgrules/26/02/rules02112639183.pdf); one trader documented $600K profit and ranked 20th on Kalshi's election leaderboard (https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/24/politics/midterm-elections-prediction-markets-kalshi-polymarket); CNBC reports traders going full-time with AI bots (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/01/traders-go-full-time-on-prediction-markets-using-ai-bots-and-antennas.html); 288 tools/terminals already catalogued with a16z backing Kairos, proving a paid-tools market (https://github.com/trevorlasn/prediction-market-trading-tools-and-terminals, https://www.bettoredge.com/post/best-prediction-market-terminals). Capital: trading bankroll is the main cost, a $50K book fits but is fully at risk. Fit for Joshua: medium-high on the tooling side (he can build a terminal/newsletter), medium on trading discipline.

name: Drone inspection + drone light-show company (Part 107 now, Part 108 BVLOS next)
thesis: Utilities, solar farms, insurers and data-center builders all need eyes in the air at $300-$700/hour, and drone shows are replacing fireworks at $15K-$100K+ per show with 60-65% margins, so one Part 107 operator can stack recurring inspection revenue with high-ticket event revenue.
who_pays: Utilities/EPCs (per-MW solar and line inspections), roofers/insurers (per roof), data-center GCs (progress mapping), and cities/venues/festivals/weddings (per show).
why_now: Drone services market $32.1B (2025) to $42.4B (2026) to $261B (2034) at 25.5% CAGR with energy the fastest-growing buyer (https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/drone-services-market-102682); inspection $300-700/hr, residential roofs $150-400, commercial $400-1,200, solar $500-1,500/MW (https://www.skyebrowse.com/news/posts/drone-services-pricing, https://dronelaunchacademy.com/resources/drone-solar-panel-inspection-2/); light shows $15-25K for 100-150 drones, $40-70K for 200-300, $100K+ for 500+, 60-65% margins (https://www.verge.aero/everything-about-drone-light-shows, https://www.illuminatedrones.com/post/startoutdoor); hybrid pyro-drone shows are the fastest-growing 2026 format (https://fireworks.org/drone-light-shows-vs-traditional-fireworks-2026-hybrid-trends/); Part 108 BVLOS final rule has been at OIRA since July 10 2026 and is expected late 2026/early 2027, unlocking routine long-range inspection (https://www.theflightbrief.com/articles/faa-part-108-bvlos-update-september-2026, https://airdata.com/blog/2026/part-108). Capital: a used thermal drone at $4-6K pays back in 15-20 roof jobs (https://www.skyebrowse.com/news/posts/drone-roof-inspection-cost); a 100+ drone show fleet costs well over $50K, no sourced fleet price found, so start with inspections and partner on shows. Fit for Joshua: medium; hail-prone Texarkana roofing and two local data-center campuses give a home market.

name: Buy a $500K-$3M HVAC/plumbing shop with SBA debt, install AI ops, sell to a PE platform
thesis: PE buys owner-operator shops at 3-5x EBITDA, bolts them onto platforms it sells at 17-20x, and the fastest way to move a shop up that ladder is exactly a call-center marketer's skill set: answer every call, book every lead, and dial maintenance agreements past 40% penetration (worth +1.5-2.5x on the multiple).
who_pays: Homeowners for service revenue today; Apex (Apollo), Wrench Group, Sila, Redwood, Champions (Blackstone) and other roll-ups at exit.
why_now: Owner-operator shops trade at 3-5x, established HVAC 4-8x, $5M+ EBITDA platforms 8-12x+ (https://risepreneur.com/exit-ready/home-services/); PE buys at 5-8x and sells platforms at 17-20x, Champions Group went to Blackstone at 18.5x (https://pipelineon.com/blog/private-equity-buying-hvac/); service-agreement penetration above 40% shifts the multiple 1.5-2.5x (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/); add-on deals landing 3.5-5x is the buy-side entry point (https://ctacquisitions.com/answers/ebitda-multiple-home-services-businesses/); deal stacks are 50-70% cash plus rollover equity (https://pipelineon.com/blog/private-equity-buying-hvac/). Capital: $50K covers the equity injection on roughly a $500K SBA 7(a) deal assuming ~10% down (standard SBA practice, not separately sourced here); bigger targets need seller notes or partners. Fit for Joshua: high on the value-creation levers, but requires operating a trades business.

name: AI UGC video-ad factory for DTC and local-service brands
thesis: Brands are shifting from $150-$300 human creator clips to AI-generated UGC at a tenth of the cost, so a shop that ships 30-50 tested ad variations per client per month on retainer keeps the margin agencies used to pay out to creators.
who_pays: DTC ecommerce brands, TikTok Shop sellers, franchises and local service companies running Meta/TikTok ads; performance agencies white-labeling the output.
why_now: US companies spent more than $10B on UGC in 2025 and the UGC platform market is ~$8.5B in 2026 (https://www.visla.us/blog/listicles/video-marketing-trends-for-2026/, https://www.hedra.com/blog/what-is-ai-ugc); a five-variation AI UGC test runs ~$100-285 vs $1,100-2,950 with human creators (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/ai-avatar-ads-vs-real-ugc-creators-cost-trust-2026); a $3K/month budget yields 3-5 human videos vs 30-50 AI variations (https://futurefactors.ai/ai-ugc-ads-2026-guide/); eMarketer projects ~$57B of AI-powered ad spend in 2026 (https://www.hoox.video/en/blog/why-brands-are-supercharging-their-campaigns-with-ai-ugc-in-2026). Sell to advertisers, not ad-revenue channels: YouTube's July-2025 'inauthentic content' policy demonetized thousands of faceless AI channels in 2026 (https://miraflow.ai/blog/youtube-monetization-ai-content-2026-allowed-demonetized). Fit for Joshua: very high, he already built a faceless-video content factory and runs paid lead gen.

name: Non-medical home-care agency with a caregiver-recruiting dialer engine
thesis: The constraint in the $174B home-care market is caregivers, not clients (500K unfilled jobs, ~77% turnover, $2,600-$5,000 per hire), so an agency that runs recruiting like a lead-gen call center fills the shifts competitors turn away and captures private-pay demand from 10,000 boomers a day turning 65.
who_pays: Private-pay families (88% of seniors want to age at home), long-term-care insurance, Medicaid HCBS waivers and the VA.
why_now: US home-care providers market ~$173.6B in 2026, +4.1% YoY (https://shiftcare.com/us/blog/private-duty-home-care-agency-growth-market-trends-service-models-2026); more than 500,000 caregiver positions unfilled, turnover near 77%, recruiting cost $2,600-$5,000 per hire, and agencies turning away clients (https://axiscare.com/blog/overcoming-caregiver-shortages-as-a-barrier-to-growth/); ~718,900 aide openings projected per year (https://senioridy.com/the-caregiver-shortage-crisis-what-families-need-to-know-in-2026/); 10,000 boomers turn 65 daily and adults 65+ outnumber children by 2034 (https://prnfunding.com/senior-boom-impacts-the-demand-for-home-healthcare-services/); profitability pressure jumped from 13% to 34% of agencies in 2026, so weak operators are exiting and consolidation buyers are active (https://www.myezcare.com/2026-home-care-industry-report-workforce-ai-adoption-growth-trends/). Fit for Joshua: high, his dialer/show-rate machinery is the missing recruiting engine; licensing and insurance are the friction.

name: Power lineworker apprentice -> journeyman on the grid/data-center buildout
thesis: Utilities are in their largest capex cycle in fifty years while postwar-generation linemen retire, so a lineworker willing to travel clears six figures with overtime within about two years of starting an apprenticeship, no degree required.
who_pays: Investor-owned utilities, co-ops and transmission contractors funded by rate base, federal grid grants and hyperscaler interconnection deals.
why_now: BLS median $95,320 (May 2025), rising to $102,550 in electric power generation/transmission/distribution (https://tradecareerpath.com/trades/lineworker/, https://lineman-jobs.com/lineman-salary); grid modernization called the quietest hiring boom in America, journeyman lead time 18 months minimum, utilities raising starting wages and poaching across regions (https://bluelinesearch.ai/insights/energy-utilities-grid-modernization-hiring-2026); the data-center rush is worsening power and grid worker shortages (https://energynow.com/2026/05/data-center-rush-worsens-shortages-of-power-grid-workers/); 28% of construction firms expect craft hiring to get harder in 2026 (https://blog.bluebeam.com/efficiency-mandate-2026-construction-labor-shortage/). Adjacent path: fiber splicers median $74,330 with 90th percentile $103,680, a 178,000-worker shortage and $42B of BEAD money (https://qualora.io/blog/fiber-optic-technician-salary-guide-2026, https://tradecolleges.org/blog/trade-programs/fiber-optic-broadband-technician-careers). Fit for Joshua: low (physical career change), included because the money is real and reachable.

name: Men's hormone-optimization telehealth brand (TRT + peptides), cash-pay membership
thesis: TRT pulls ~246,000 US searches a month, 40% of men under 40 say they want it but only 14% have tried it, and white-label telehealth stacks let a marketer-operator run a cash-pay membership clinic just as the compounded-GLP-1 crowd lost its product and needs a new offer.
who_pays: Men 30-60 paying monthly cash memberships covering labs, Rx and peptide adjuncts; no insurance dependency.
why_now: TRT ~246K monthly searches with 40% interest vs 14% usage among men under 40 (https://altosconsultinggroup.com/post/hormone-optimization-clinic-business-opportunity-2026); global TRT market ~$1.9B (2024) and peptides ~$117B growing 10.8% CAGR (https://openloophealth.com/blog/the-top-telehealth-services-providers-should-add-on-in-2026); telehealth TRT delivery growing 5.88% CAGR through 2031 (https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/testosterone-replacement-therapy-market); Forbes on men's wellness clinics scaling concierge models in 2026 (https://www.forbes.com/sites/tanyaakim/2026/02/20/the-mens-wellness-clinics-scaling-a-new-concierge-like-model/); comparable semaglutide brands net $9-18K/month at 100 patients and $45-90K at 500 (https://karpahealth.com/resources/semaglutide-telehealth-brand-launch/), but FDA moved in April 2026 to pull semaglutide/tirzepatide from the 503B bulks list and major compounders quit (https://trytrimi.com/blog/best-compounded-glp1-providers), which is why TRT/peptides, not GLP-1, is the 2026 entry point. Capital: needs an MSO/physician-owned structure and licensed prescribers; no sourced startup figure, likely $25-75K (estimate; basis: white-label platform, legal setup and initial ad spend). Fit for Joshua: high on acquisition/retention marketing, low on clinical, so it is a partner-with-a-provider play.

name: Septic pumping + real-estate septic inspection route
thesis: One used vacuum truck on a rural route bills $300-500 per pump-out and $350-600 per transfer inspection, runs 4-8 jobs a day with near-zero marketing because the sewage does not stop, and the roll-ups (Wind River, PE-backed regionals) pay 1.5-2.5x revenue for routes when you want out.
who_pays: Rural homeowners (one in five US homes is on septic, far higher around Texarkana), realtors and lenders who need an inspection to close, landlords and RV parks with on-site systems.
why_now: Rural Ark-La-Tex housing stock is aging past the 30-year life of its drainfields, county health departments and lenders increasingly require point-of-sale septic inspections, and the incumbents are 60-year-old owner-operators with no succession plan and no online presence. Real capital number: $60-90K for a used vac truck plus TCEQ/ADH licensing, so slightly above the $50K assumption.

name: Used cooking oil collection + grease trap pumping route
thesis: Restaurants pay you to pump their grease traps, then you collect their used cooking oil for free and sell it into the renewable-diesel supply chain at roughly $0.40-0.55 per pound, so a 200-restaurant route produces two revenue streams off one truck and one driver.
who_pays: Restaurants, hospitals, schools and RV-park kitchens pay for trap service; renewable-diesel and biodiesel aggregators (Darling/DAR PRO, regional buyers) pay for the oil.
why_now: The 45Z clean fuel credit was extended through 2029 and renewable-diesel capacity keeps sucking up every pound of domestic UCO, cities are tightening FOG (fats, oils, grease) enforcement on restaurants, and the national collectors underserve small-market routes like Texarkana where a local truck can lock up exclusive contracts.

name: Diesel generator load-bank testing and fuel polishing for data centers, hospitals and telecom sites
thesis: NFPA 110 and Joint Commission rules require annual load-bank tests and clean fuel on every backup generator, each visit bills $1,500-6,000, and there are thousands of new generators being installed across Texas and the South with almost no independent local testers.
who_pays: Data-center operators and their facilities contractors, hospitals, cell-tower owners, municipal water plants, Class A office landlords, and generator dealers who subcontract testing.
why_now: ERCOT's large-load queue has exploded past 100 GW of data-center and industrial requests, every one of those sites is installing rows of diesel gensets that must be tested and have fuel polished on a schedule, and the OEM service networks are backlogged months. Capital: $40-70K for a trailer-mounted resistive load bank and a fuel-polishing rig.

name: Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation (NEMT) wheelchair-van operation
thesis: Each wheelchair or stretcher trip pays $40-150 through the state's managed transportation organization, a single van runs 8-14 billable trips a day, and demand is guaranteed by law because Medicaid must get members to dialysis, chemo and appointments.
who_pays: Texas Medicaid MTOs and Arkansas brokers (MTM, Modivcare, ModivCare-style intermediaries), Medicare Advantage plans, hospitals discharging patients, and private-pay families.
why_now: Rural provider shortages are so severe that brokers are paying enhanced rates and signing anyone with a compliant van, 4 million Americans hit 65 every year through 2027, and dialysis clinic expansion in small markets creates fixed three-times-a-week routes. Real capital: $75-110K for two used ADA vans plus insurance, above the $50K baseline.

name: Regulated medical waste pickup route (sharps, red-bag, pharma) for small clinics
thesis: Dentists, vets, tattoo shops, dialysis centers, urgent cares and nursing homes each pay $80-400 per month on multi-year contracts for a legally mandated pickup, so 300 accounts on a cargo-van route is $500K+ of subscription revenue with a licensing moat that keeps casual competitors out.
who_pays: Dental and medical practices, veterinary clinics, tattoo and med-spa studios, long-term-care facilities, county jails, and funeral homes.
why_now: Waste Management swallowed Stericycle in late 2024 and small accounts are getting price hikes, auto-renewal contracts and worse service, which is the classic moment for a local operator to churn them; TCEQ registration plus a treatment-facility subcontract is a paperwork moat, not a capital moat (roughly $35-60K to start).

name: Foreclosure and tax-sale surplus-funds recovery
thesis: When a home is sold at a tax or mortgage foreclosure for more than what was owed, the excess sits with the county or trustee unclaimed; you locate the former owner or heirs by skip-tracing and phone, file the claim for them, and keep a contingency fee on checks that are routinely $5K-$80K.
who_pays: Former homeowners and their heirs, out of the surplus itself (Texas caps tax-sale assignments at 25%; mortgage-foreclosure surplus in Texas and most states is less restricted), plus attorneys who pay finder fees.
why_now: Foreclosure filings climbed through 2025-2026 as post-COVID forbearance ended and insurance-driven cost spikes squeezed Sun Belt owners, county lists are now published online, and almost nobody in the Ark-La-Tex runs a professional, compliant operation; this is a dialer-and-skip-trace business, which is Joshua's exact operating skill, with under $10K capital.

name: Licensed public adjuster for hail, wind and freeze claims
thesis: A Texas public adjuster represents the policyholder against the carrier and legally earns up to 10% of the settlement, so a single hail-damaged commercial roof or a $150K freeze-burst loss pays $6K-$15K, and one good storm season across Texas produces $200K-$500K for a solo operator with a couple of field inspectors.
who_pays: Homeowners, HOAs, apartment owners, churches, and small commercial property owners whose claims were underpaid or denied, out of the recovered settlement.
why_now: Carriers have been using AI-driven desk adjusting and aggressive depreciation to shrink payouts, Texas homeowner premiums rose 40%+ in three years so owners are furious and litigious, and the license takes a state exam plus a $10K bond rather than a degree; roofers cannot legally negotiate claims, leaving the lane wide open.

name: Commercial (B2B) collections agency for contractors, trucking and medical practices
thesis: Small businesses write off billions in unpaid invoices every year because they have no one to chase them; a bonded agency working 25-35% contingency on $5K-$100K commercial debts is a pure dialer-and-demand-letter operation with margins above 50% and no inventory.
who_pays: Subcontractors, HVAC and plumbing companies, freight carriers, staffing firms, and physician groups assign their receivables; the debtor business pays.
why_now: 2025-2026 tightening credit and rising insolvencies among small contractors and carriers created a backlog of 90-day-plus receivables, commercial collections is exempt from most consumer FDCPA restrictions, and Texas only requires a $10K bond and Secretary of State registration; Joshua already runs dialers, reps and scripts, which is the whole business.

name: AI-assisted payer credentialing and enrollment service for independent clinics
thesis: Every new provider has to be enrolled with 10-25 insurance payers before they can bill, each enrollment takes 90-180 days of forms, CAQH upkeep and follow-up calls, practices pay $150-400 per application plus $50-100 per provider per month for maintenance, and an AI-scripted intake plus a phone follow-up rep can run 10x the volume of the typical credentialing coordinator.
who_pays: Independent physician practices, nurse-practitioner-owned clinics, therapy and behavioral-health groups, dental groups, and rural hospitals staffing locums.
why_now: Nurse practitioners and PAs are opening independent clinics in record numbers across full-practice-authority states, Medicaid and Medicare revalidation cycles keep expanding, credentialing staff are burned out and quitting, and LLM tooling now handles the document assembly that used to require a human for every form; Joshua can build the workflow software himself and sell it by phone.

name: Estate cleanout, hoarder and unattended-death cleanup company
thesis: Heirs, executors, landlords and realtors pay $2K-$15K per job to make a house empty and sellable fast, hoarder and biohazard jobs run $5K-$30K with insurance often covering them, and the labor is a trailer, a dumpster account, PPE and two crew members.
who_pays: Executors and adult children of the deceased, probate attorneys, property managers and landlords, banks and REO agents, and homeowner or landlord insurance policies for biohazard remediation.
why_now: The largest generation in US history is hitting its mortality peak over the next decade with houses full of 50 years of stuff, kids live in other states and cannot take a week off to sort it, and the incumbents are junk haulers who will not touch the sensitive, embarrassing, or biological jobs that carry the highest margins.

name: Performance-based no-show reduction and dormant-patient reactivation service for dental and medical practices
thesis: Medical and dental no-shows cost US practices an estimated $150B a year and a 20-30% no-show rate is normal; a dedicated confirmation, rescheduling and reactivation call team charging per kept appointment or a monthly retainer converts a dead chart list into $50K-$200K of recovered production per practice per year and takes a cut.
who_pays: Dental practices, dermatology, physical therapy, chiropractic, orthodontics, med-spas and any appointment-based clinic; larger DSOs and MSOs pay enterprise retainers.
why_now: Practices replaced front-desk callers with text reminders that patients ignore, private-equity-owned dental and PT groups are under pressure to raise chair utilization, and AI dialers plus a small human team can run confirmations, wait-list backfill and recall campaigns at a cost no practice can match in-house; it is literally Joshua's show-rate discipline pointed at a bigger, higher-margin vertical.

name: Fiber-optic splicing technician on BEAD-funded rural broadband builds
thesis: Certified fusion splicers earn $35-70 per hour or $150-300 per splice case on contract, with per-diem and overtime pushing experienced techs past $120K a year, and the skill is learnable in weeks through a splicing course or an ISP's own training, not a degree.
who_pays: Electric co-ops, rural telcos and ISPs building last-mile fiber, and the engineering contractors (Dycom, MasTec, regional outfits) who hire crews and 1099 subcontractors.
why_now: The $42.5B BEAD program restarted after its 2025 restructuring and the construction money flows in 2026-2028, with Texas and Arkansas among the biggest allocations; every one of those thousands of route-miles needs splicing, and the labor pool is so thin that contractors are paying signing bonuses and per-diem to anyone with a fusion splicer certificate and a clean driving record.

name: Show-Rate Guarantee Desk for high-ticket consult businesses
thesis: Med spas, dental-implant and ortho centers, LASIK, solar/roofing/HVAC-replacement sales, and membership-tour operators lose 25-40% of booked consults to no-shows; an outsourced confirmation-and-rescue desk (AI voice + SMS first-pass confirmations, deposit capture, human rescue calls, same-day waitlist backfill, rebook-on-cancel) sold at $40-150 per kept appointment or a $3-8K/mo retainer can clear $1-3M/yr with 15-25 seats of cheap Texarkana labor, because one kept implant or solar consult is worth $3-8K to the client and they already measure show rate as a KPI.
who_pays: Owners and marketing directors of high-ticket consult businesses: med-spa chains, dental implant/ortho groups, solar and roofing sales orgs, HVAC replacement dealers, RV-resort/timeshare tour operators, and the marketing agencies that book for them.
why_now: AI voice agents now do first-pass confirmations for roughly $0.10/min, consumer no-show rates never recovered after 2020, and every lead-gen client is paying more per booked appointment as ad costs rise, so a guaranteed-show layer is the cheapest lift available. Joshua runs this exact function today (dialers, reps, show rates) and can sell it as a productized service on day one.

name: Contingency denial-recovery and appeals shop for independent practices
thesis: Claim denial rates run 12-15% and most denied claims are never re-worked because the practice cannot afford the 45 minutes per appeal; a firm that takes only aged and denied claims, writes payer-specific, clinically cited appeals with AI, and has humans work the phone and prior-auth follow-ups, paid 20-30% of dollars recovered, can pull $2-5M/yr from 30-50 practice clients at 50%+ margin because the AI turns a 45-minute appeal into a 5-minute review.
who_pays: Independent physician groups, PT/chiro/behavioral-health practices, ambulatory surgery centers, rural hospitals and FQHCs; the practice manager or CFO signs a contingency agreement with zero upfront cost.
why_now: Payers now auto-deny with AI (UnitedHealth, Cigna, Humana litigation), the CMS 2026 prior-authorization interoperability rule and WISeR model add new friction, 2026 Medicare fee cuts squeeze margins, and LLMs finally write medical-necessity appeals that cite policy and clinical guidelines well enough to win.

name: Small-landlord maintenance-coordination desk with vetted-vendor dispatch
thesis: Individual landlords own roughly 40% of US rental units and have no maintenance desk, so tenants text the owner at 11pm and contractors ghost; a 24/7 line (AI triage, dispatch of pre-vetted tradespeople who post a deposit and get photo-verified completion, owner approval by text) charging $25-40 per door per month plus 15-20% on jobs turns 3,000 doors into $1.5-2.5M/yr with almost no capex and a national footprint from one Texarkana office.
who_pays: Mom-and-pop landlords with 1-20 units, self-managed HOAs, and small property-management firms that white-label the desk instead of hiring a coordinator.
why_now: Contractor reliability is the number-one landlord complaint as trade labor stays scarce, AI phone agents make a real 24/7 desk cheap for the first time, and flat rents with rising insurance and taxes push owners to buy a $30/door service rather than an 8-10% full-management fee.

name: Remote permit-expediting service for small contractors across TX/AR/LA/OK
thesis: Every solar, pool, roof, ADU, sign, restaurant build-out and remodel job waits weeks on permits and contractors despise the desk work; an expediter who files, tracks, and chases across dozens of municipal portals at $350-2,500 per permit or a $500-1,500/mo per-contractor retainer bills $300-600K solo and $1-2M with four staff, with an internal tracking tool as the moat and eventual software product.
who_pays: General contractors, solar/roofing/pool installers, restaurant and franchise build-out teams, sign companies, and homeowners doing ADUs; they pay per permit or per month and pass the cost to the customer.
why_now: Texas HB 14 (third-party plan review when cities miss deadlines) and 2025's SB 840 / HB 24 zoning reforms are unlocking more infill, ADU and conversion projects while city permit desks stay understaffed; post-storm rebuilding across the Ark-La-Tex adds volume; and municipal portals are fragmented enough that aggregation is a paid service rather than a feature anyone has built.

name: Licensed public adjuster for hail, wind and water claims in the Ark-La-Tex storm belt
thesis: Homeowners and small commercial owners are routinely underpaid 30-60% on storm claims; a Texas-licensed public adjuster (fast exam, low fee) takes up to the 10% statutory cap of the settlement, and one storm season of 40-60 roof, commercial and church claims averaging $40-120K each yields $250-600K per adjuster, then scales into a firm with commission-only adjusters and AI-drafted Xactimate estimates and demand packages.
who_pays: Policyholders, paid out of the settlement itself with nothing out of pocket; commercial owners, apartment complexes, churches and schools are the biggest tickets, and roofers and restoration contractors feed referrals.
why_now: Carriers are using AI claim triage and mass non-renewals, 2024-26 produced record severe-convective-storm losses across TX/OK/AR, underpayment and denial rates are at multi-decade highs, and AI now cuts estimate-writing labor by roughly 80%, so a one-person shop can carry a firm's caseload.

name: Executor's Assistant: flat-fee estate-settlement admin ('death admin') service
thesis: Settling an estate takes an executor hundreds of hours over 12-18 months of calls to banks, SSA, DMV, utilities, brokerages, subscriptions and creditors; a non-legal executor's-assistant service that runs the checklist, makes the calls, closes accounts, and packages paperwork for the attorney at $3-7K flat per estate (paid from the estate) can handle 150-300 estates a year with a small team for $1-2M, with the checklist software as the wedge and a national remote footprint.
who_pays: Executors and heirs via estate funds; funeral homes, probate attorneys, financial advisors and trust officers are the referral channel because they hate doing this work and cannot bill for it.
why_now: The $84 trillion wealth transfer is underway and US deaths climb through 2026-2035 as boomers age; VC-backed Empathy and Alix proved the demand but sell through employers and insurers, leaving direct-to-executor, rural and Southern markets wide open; AI assembles the letters, forms and account inventories that used to make this unprofitable.

name: Contingency accounts-receivable recovery desk for contractors and subcontractors
thesis: Construction carries roughly a quarter-trillion dollars in late receivables and the average subcontractor waits 80+ days to get paid; a pre-litigation AR desk that runs AI-written dunning cadences, files preliminary lien and bond-claim notices, and makes human collection calls, taking 15-25% of collected dollars or a $500-2K/mo retainer, does $1-3M/yr on 100 clients because every trade contractor has $50-500K sitting uncollected and no one on staff to chase it.
who_pays: Subcontractors and specialty trades, equipment rental yards, commercial cleaning, landscaping, and other B2B service firms with net-30 invoices that turn into net-120.
why_now: 2025-26 payment delays hit record highs as construction credit tightened, lien-notice and prompt-payment statutes give real leverage, AI personalizes demand sequences at near-zero cost, and Texarkana phone labor plus Joshua's dialer operations make the human layer cheap and scalable.

name: FMCSA compliance-in-a-box for 1-20 truck fleets
thesis: About 90% of US carriers run fewer than ten trucks and most fail their first audit on driver-qualification files, drug-and-alcohol consortium enrollment, ELD/HOS records, and IFTA; a $150-300 per truck per month done-for-you compliance service (AI keeps DQ files audit-ready, humans handle roadside violations, DataQs challenges, new-entrant audits and IRP/IFTA filings) reaches $1.5-3M ARR at 1,000 trucks with sticky retention because losing operating authority ends the business.
who_pays: Owner-operators and small fleet owners, plus the small-fleet insurers, factoring companies and dispatch services that want lower-risk clients and will refer or bundle.
why_now: FMCSA's 2025-26 enforcement wave (English-proficiency out-of-service rule, non-domiciled CDL crackdown, Clearinghouse-II, registration-system overhaul) has small carriers terrified of audits and revocations; AI document handling makes per-truck pricing profitable; and Texarkana sits on the I-30/I-49 freight corridor surrounded by exactly these fleets.

name: Automated Texas property-tax protest firm for homeowners and small commercial owners
thesis: Texas has no income tax so property-tax bills are enormous, yet the large majority of owners never protest; a licensed property-tax consultant who mass-files protests with AI-built comparable-sales and unequal-appraisal evidence and settles informally with appraisal districts, charging 25-40% of first-year savings, runs 10-20K accounts with three people, and at a $300-500 average fee that is $3-6M/yr (Ownwell and Home Tax Shield scaled to nine-figure valuations on this exact model).
who_pays: Homeowners, landlords and small commercial owners on pure contingency (no savings, no fee), acquired cheaply by direct mail and digital ads keyed to appraisal-notice season.
why_now: 2024-26 appraisal spikes across DFW, Austin, Houston and San Antonio, the 2025 homestead-exemption increase made owners scrutinize bills, Texas consultant licensing is a quick exam, and AI comps plus e-filing collapse the cost per account to a few dollars, so the whole state is addressable from Texarkana.

name: Workers'-comp premium-audit recovery consultancy (contingency) for SMBs
thesis: A large share of workers'-comp policies contain class-code, payroll, subcontractor, or experience-mod errors that overcharge employers by $5-50K a year; a recovery consultant who audits the last three to five years, files for refunds and mod corrections with the carrier and rating bureau, and keeps 30-50% of dollars recovered closes $8-20K per win and can bill $1M+ solo on cold outbound to roofers, framers, staffing firms, trucking and manufacturers, with no fee unless money comes back.
who_pays: Employers with $75K+ annual premiums in high-rate classes: roofing, framing, staffing agencies, trucking, manufacturing, nursing homes, and municipalities; the CFO or owner signs a contingency letter.
why_now: 2024-26 payroll inflation and NCCI class-code updates left stale classifications and mods everywhere, AI reads audit worksheets and rating manuals in seconds, and neither the agent nor the carrier is paid to find the overcharge, so the market is un-mined and Joshua's outbound machine is the exact acquisition engine.

name: Orphaned-solar rescue: O&M, repair and warranty-claim service for abandoned residential solar systems
thesis: The 2024-26 installer bankruptcy wave (SunPower, Lumio, Titan, Sunnova, Meyer Burger and thousands of local dealers) orphaned hundreds of thousands of residential systems whose owners still owe 20-year loans on panels nobody will service; a diagnostics-and-repair company that fixes inverters and optimizers, files manufacturer warranty claims for paid labor, sells $25-40/mo monitoring, and performs lender- and home-sale-required repairs can clear $2-5M/yr per metro with two electrician crews and AI-run claims paperwork.
who_pays: Homeowners out of pocket, inverter and panel manufacturers (Enphase, SolarEdge, Tesla) via warranty labor reimbursement, solar lenders and PPA owners (GoodLeap, Mosaic, Sunrun) who need collateral producing, and home sellers and realtors who need a working system to close.
why_now: The residential solar tax credit (25D) ended December 31, 2025, collapsing new installs and killing more installers, while roughly five million existing systems age into inverter-failure years; service demand is rising exactly as installer supply disappears and nobody has built the national 'we'll fix anyone's system' brand.

name: Outbound deliverability and TCPA-compliance ops for lead-gen call centers
thesis: Contact rates across outbound centers collapsed as carriers spam-label DIDs and TCPA and state mini-TCPA suits exploded; a managed service that runs DID reputation remediation and rotation, STIR/SHAKEN attestation and branded calling, consent-proof audits, litigator scrubs, and dialer configuration for $3-10K/mo per client carries 20-40 clients for $1-3M/yr with Joshua's exact skill set, and a five-point contact-rate lift or one avoided class action is worth six figures to each client.
who_pays: Lead-gen call centers, solar, insurance, debt-relief and home-services dialer shops, BPOs, and franchise marketing groups that live or die on connect rates and cannot afford a $500K TCPA settlement.
why_now: The 2025 vacatur of the FCC one-to-one consent rule created regulatory whiplash, states passed a wave of mini-TCPAs, carriers tightened spam-scoring and branded-calling requirements, and AI dialers flooded the network with bad-actor volume, so legitimate operators need a specialist to keep dialing profitably and there are very few people who have actually run the seats and the dialer.

name: Lithium-corridor crew camp: 60-80 pad monthly workforce RV park between Texarkana and Lewisville/Magnolia AR (converts to hunting/RV resort after the build)
thesis: Three lithium plants and an $18B data-center hub are about to drop 2,000+ construction workers into counties with almost no lodging, and a workforce RV park rents pads at $525-875/month all-in (https://www.vintonrvresort.com/workforce-housing-near-lake-charles-refineries-and-industrial-sites-the-complete-2026-rv-living-guide, https://diamondvalleyrvpark.com/specialty-audiences/why-construction-workers-and-tradespeople-are-choosing-rv-parks/), so 60 pads at ~$650 is ~$470K/yr of near-100%-occupancy revenue on an asset that trades at an 8.5-10% cap (https://www.sba504blog.com/sba-loan-rv-park-workforce-housing/), i.e. a $4-5M park built for $1.5-2.5M (engineered pads $40-70K each, rural 10-25% cheaper: https://software.roverpass.com/blog/rv-park-costs, https://propertybuild.com/rv-park-construction/) — REAL CAPITAL NEED: ~$1.5-2.5M total with ~$150-250K equity via SBA 7(a), not $50K; Joshua's RV-resort operations background is the unfair advantage, and the exit is flipping it to a deer/duck-season RV resort on Ark-La-Tex timber land where lodging is the top value driver for hunting leases (https://www.texashuntingleaselistings.com/the-field-guide/texas-hunting-leases-spring-turkey-hunts-january-2026).
who_pays: EPC contractors and their per-diem-funded crews: S&B Engineers (central plant) and Wood Group (well field) on the $1.5B Smackover Lithium project (400-500 construction jobs, https://www.magnoliabannernews.com/news/2026/sep/21/smackover-lithium-lays-out-15b-project-plans/, https://www.knoe.com/2026/09/22/south-arkansas-brine-emerges-ground-zero-us-lithium-supply-national-defense/), ExxonMobil's Columbia County plant (https://www.kark.com/news/state-news/gov-sarah-huckabee-sanders-to-make-economic-announcement/), TerraVolta/Chevron's $1B+ Liberty Owl in Miller County (https://www.terravolta.com/news/terravolta-resources-selected-by-us-department-of-energy-for-225-million-award-negotiation-for-lithium-production-facility-in-texarkana-region), Stack Infrastructure's 1,500 Amazon construction workers in Shreveport-Bossier (https://www.constructiondive.com/news/amazon-louisiana-data-center-construction/813021/), plus traveling nurses and RRAD supplemental-labor contractors ($20-40/hr, https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Red-River-Army-Depot).
why_now: Smackover Lithium laid out its $1.5B plan on Sept 21, 2026 with major construction starting early 2027 and first production 2029 (https://www.magnoliabannernews.com/news/2026/sep/21/smackover-lithium-lays-out-15b-project-plans/); ExxonMobil targets a 2027 facility (https://www.kark.com/news/state-news/gov-sarah-huckabee-sanders-to-make-economic-announcement/); TerraVolta breaks ground 2028 (https://www.terravolta.com/news/terravolta-resources-selected-by-us-department-of-energy-for-225-million-award-negotiation-for-lithium-production-facility-in-texarkana-region); Amazon raised NW Louisiana to $18B/three campuses in Aug 2026 (https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-data-center-louisiana-new-jobs); and Texarkana's own mayor calls workforce housing a shortage the region must solve (https://www.txkmag.com/news/community-culture/housing-texarkana/). Pads built in 2026-27 are full before the first plant pours concrete.

name: Septic (OSSF) + water-well installation company for the west Bowie County / Miller County subdivision sprawl
thesis: Texarkana's housing review says west-side subdivisions are being forced onto wells and septic because utility expansion hasn't kept pace (https://www.txkmag.com/news/community-culture/housing-texarkana/), and every one of those lots is a $10-20K aerobic septic ticket (https://dillonseptic.com/aerobic-septic-system-cost-in-texas/) plus a $6-30K well (https://drillerdb.com/resources/well-owner/texas-well-guide) plus a mandatory $300-500/yr aerobic maintenance contract that compounds into recurring revenue (https://www.texassepticguide.com/learn/septic-maintenance-cost-texas) — two crews doing three installs a week is a $1.5-3M/yr business (estimate: 150 installs x $10-20K), entered with a TEEX Installer I course that requires no prior experience (https://teex.org/class/www302/) and where even employee Installer II roles post at $75-100K (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Ossf/-in-Austin,TX).
who_pays: Spec and custom homebuilders on the west side, land buyers subdividing pasture, new residents relocating for RRAD/CHRISTUS/lithium jobs, and every aerobic-system owner paying the TCEQ-required maintenance contract each year.
why_now: Texarkana home values rose 2.8% in the year to June 2026 and the city is waiving permit fees and streamlining inspections to force more housing starts (https://www.zillow.com/home-values/20782/texarkana-tx/, https://www.txkmag.com/news/community-culture/housing-texarkana/), while Texas needs 530K+ additional trades workers in 2026 (https://www.metaintro.com/blog/skilled-trade-jobs-construction-electrical-plumbing-careers-2026) — the bottleneck is installers, not lots. Starting capital ~$50K works with a financed used mini-excavator/backhoe and trailer (estimate based on used-equipment pricing; no direct source).

name: Secured monthly truck yard + on-site mobile DOT inspection/PM shop at the I-30 / US-59 / TexAmericas Center hub
thesis: There is roughly one legal truck parking space for every 11 drivers nationally (https://www.newsnationnow.com/politics/trump-veteran-trucker-shortage/), TxDOT is spending $10.6M to add only 175 public spaces west of Texarkana and won't finish until Feb 2028 (https://www.texarkanagazette.com/news/2026/sep/13/txdot-project-to-provide-parking-for-commercial/), and secured monthly parking rents for $150-350/space (https://www.recnationstorage.com/blog/how-much-is-truck-parking-parking-rates-explained/) — so a 100-space fenced, lit, camera-monitored gravel yard near TexAmericas Center (3PL tenant base up 67%, employment up 136% in five years: https://txktoday.com/news/texamericas-center-retains-no-5-industrial-park-ranking-2026/) throws off $240-360K/yr recurring before layering on annual DOT inspections at $125-165 each (https://mightyfleetservices.com/2026/04/25/annual-dot-inspections-cost-guide/), PM service, and tire/reefer work for the small fleets and log-truck owner-operators who have nowhere to park at home. Capital: ~$250-500K for land, fence, lighting, cameras (estimate; land price and site work not sourced), owner-financeable.
who_pays: Owner-operators and 5-30 truck fleets domiciled in the 17-county trade area, TexAmericas Center 3PL tenants, log haulers serving Domtar/Graphic Packaging, and carriers staging for the lithium and Amazon builds; the federal government is also putting $200M/yr into truck parking in FY2026-27 (https://www.fleetowner.com/perspectives/ideaxchange/blog/55401528/truck-parking-crisis-safety-costs-and-other-fleet-risks).
why_now: TxDOT's Sept 2026 award proves the shortage is acute on this exact stretch of I-30 (https://www.ktbs.com/news/texarkana/txdot-moves-forward-with-major-truck-parking-project-along-i-30-in-east-texas/article_93deef48-b33a-412f-8000-7fd6f19503c3.html), TexAmericas is expanding its transload area as the only transload hub within 80-100 miles (https://www.newbostontx.org/TexAmerica-Center-Spotlights.html), and new spaces cost $100-200K each to build publicly (https://blog.semiyard.com/why-its-getting-harder-to-find-truck-parking-in-2026-and-what-you-can-do-about-it/) — a private gravel yard undercuts that by 10x and rents out before the public lot opens.

name: Buy the retiring owner's HVAC/plumbing/septic/pest company in a 5K-30K-person Ark-La-Tex town with an SBA 7(a) loan, then bolt on modern marketing and dispatch
thesis: Trades businesses sell at 2.5-3.2x seller's discretionary earnings with the median deal at $350K on $165K SDE (https://joinaccredited.com/blog/best-small-businesses-to-buy-2026), SBA 7(a) allows 10% down on deals up to $5M (https://joinaccredited.com/blog/best-small-businesses-to-buy-2026), so ~$50K controls a ~$500K rural business paying its owner $165K+ from day one, and small-town sellers face far fewer bidders than the metro firms where PE has bought ~800 HVAC/plumbing/electrical companies since 2022 (https://www.inc.com/victoria-salves/millennials-buying-up-hvac-and-plumbing-companies/91368971) — Joshua's lead-gen, dialer, and rep-management skills applied to a business that currently has no CRM, no follow-up, and no online presence can plausibly double SDE inside 24 months.
who_pays: The acquired company's existing service-contract and repeat-customer base across Bowie, Miller, Cass, Little River, Hempstead and Lafayette counties; the seller often carries 10-15% of the note.
why_now: Boomers still own ~12 million private companies with mostly no succession plan (https://www.clearlyacquired.com/blog/silver-tsunami-what-it-means-for-buyers), SBA-backed acquisition loans hit a record 6,915 loans / $8.17B in FY2025 (https://www.marketingcode.com/industry-shift-forbes-millennials-blue-collar-ai-proof-6915-sba-loans-jul-2026/), and 2026 is described as the Silver Tsunami's peak (https://sugarland.fcbb.com/news/sugar-land-businesses-for-sale-retiring-owners) — rural Texas/Arkansas trades owners in their late 60s are the least-contested inventory in the country.

name: Forestry-mulching + pasture-conversion + fencing crew: turn worthless pine into record-priced cattle pasture
thesis: Pine sawtimber and pulpwood are at their lowest prices in 25 years and five Arkansas wood plants closed or idled in 2025 (https://www.uaex.uada.edu/media-resources/news/2026/january/01-26-2026-UAM-forestry-opinion.aspx) while feeder calves are $437/cwt heading to $467 (https://texasfarmbureau.org/strong-demand-high-cattle-prices-to-continue-for-ranchers/, https://fortune.com/2026/08/11/record-beef-cow-calf-ranchers-feedlot-farmers/), so landowners across the Ark-La-Tex are converting overstocked timber to pasture — and the contractor gets paid at every step: mulching $1,500-5,000/acre (https://bearclawclearing.com/texas/forestry-mulching-cost), barbed-wire fence $4.25-7.25/ft in Texas (https://bhumicalculator.com/countries/united-states/barbed-wire-fence-cost-per-foot), pipe fence $13.50-40/ft (https://www.angi.com/articles/horse-fencing-cost.htm); one track-loader/mulcher package (MachineryTrader average $97K, range $20-194K: https://www.machinerytrader.com/listings/for-sale/skid-steer-mulchers-forestry-equipment/31458) clearing ~2 acres/day at ~$2,500/acre grosses ~$1M/yr at 200 working days (estimate; utilization not sourced), financeable with $50K down.
who_pays: Timber-tract owners, cow-calf ranchers expanding herds into record prices, hunting-lease operators wanting food plots and shooting lanes, homebuilders clearing west-side lots, and utilities/fiber contractors needing right-of-way clearing.
why_now: A year-plus drought has stressed Arkansas timber stands and cut harvests (https://www.uaex.uada.edu/media-resources/news/2026/june/06-29-2026-ark-timber-drought.aspx), overstocked forests now face insect and wildfire risk (https://www.uaex.uada.edu/media-resources/news/2026/january/01-26-2026-UAM-forestry-opinion.aspx), Texas herds are the smallest since 1952 (https://www.houstonpublicmedia.org/articles/economy/2026/03/11/545836/beef-price-texas-farmer-rancher-restaurant-houston-rodeo/), and forestry mulching is 20-40% cheaper than dozer clearing so it wins the bid (https://corralbros.com/blog/land-clearing-cost-per-acre-texas/).

name: BEAD last-mile fiber subcontractor: directional-boring and drop-bury crews for the Texas and Arkansas broadband build
thesis: Texas's $3.31B BEAD program is the largest fiber build in US history with 8,000-12,000 peak construction workers and builds running through 2030 (https://buildermuse.com/infrastructure/broadband-infrastructure-42-billion-bead-program-finally/), Arkansas's $1.02B program is 76% fiber with construction starting H1 2026 (https://broadband.arkansas.gov/bead/), civil contractors who can bore and splice are booked 18 months out (https://buildermuse.com/infrastructure/broadband-contracts-new-revenue-stream-contractors/), and directional boring bills $20-30/ft with a $15-50 range (https://www.excavatinginsurancepartners.com/post/directional-drilling-rates-fiber-optic-2025) — a two-person bore crew producing 400-500 ft/day is $8-15K/day gross (estimate), and a drop-bury crew can start for under $50K while the bore rig ($100-200K used, estimate) is financed.
who_pays: BEAD subgrantee ISPs and their prime contractors: Spectrum/Charter is already securing right-of-way in its Texas award counties (https://www.shovels.ai/blog/texas-bead-new-construction/), Arkansas winners include Hometown Internet ($88.5M, 16,056 locations) and Aristotle ($69M, 9,420 locations) (https://www.telecompetitor.com/updated-comprehensive-list-bead-benefit-of-the-bargain-provisional-awards/), plus electric co-ops and the Arkansas Rural Connect program.
why_now: Arkansas approved its first $126M tranche for 51,000 homes in Feb 2026 (https://www.arkansasbusiness.com/article/126-million-bead-awards-approved/), Texas finalized subgrantee contracts and is mobilizing contractors now (https://fibercontractorinsurance.com/blog/bead-program-fiber-contractor-opportunity-2026/), and four Texas winners rescinded 31,000 locations in June 2026 (https://broadbandbreakfast.com/winning-bidders-back-out-of-31-000-bead-locations-in-texas/) — those locations get re-awarded on compressed timelines, which is exactly when subs name their price.

name: Acquire an existing Medicare-certified home health or hospice agency in the Texarkana trade area while the CMS moratorium blocks all new entrants
thesis: CMS froze all new Medicare enrollments for home health and hospice nationwide on May 13, 2026, for six months extendable in six-month increments (https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/05/cms-announces-nationwide-enrollment-moratoria), law firms say this drives up the scarcity value of existing agencies with clean enrollment histories (https://www.nixonpeabody.com/insights/alerts/2026/05/14/cms-hospice-and-home-health-agency-moratorium-impact-on-ma-and-ownership-changes), yet small certified Texas agencies are still listed at $180K-$365K (https://dealstream.com/texas/home-health-care-businesses-for-sale) and $275K (https://americanhealthcarecapital.com/listing/txmc8z/) — buy one enrolled more than 36 months (the ownership-change rule exempts it: https://www.polsinelli.com/publications/hospice-home-health-providers-medicare-enrollment-moratoria), then use marketing-ops skill to grow census in a 17-county rural area with an aging population and a critical primary-care shortage in Arkansas (https://healthy.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/Office_of_Rural_Health_and_Primary_Care_Primary_Care_Needs_Assessment.pdf). REAL CAPITAL NEED: $200-400K purchase plus working capital, SBA-financeable.
