thesis: PE platforms that bought roughly 800 HVAC/plumbing/electrical shops run CSR book rates of 50-75% with only 35% of agents asking for the booking, so a 90-day book-rate turnaround ($25K-60K per platform) followed by a managed overflow/after-hours/outbound rehash desk priced per booked job ($15-40 each) converts directly into EBITDA the sponsor is hunting for.
who_pays: Private-equity-backed home-services platforms and $10M-50M independents on ServiceTitan, sponsored by the PE operating partner or the platform COO.
why_now: The 'roll-up of the roll-ups' is expected within 18 months, forcing platforms to show operating gains before sale; the home-services gold rush is over and 'who can actually run a business' is the 2026 story; ServiceTitan Contact Center Pro case studies show 13% booking lifts but require operators to realize them.

name: Ex-Solar Sales Force Redeployed into a Pay-Per-Appointment Call Center for Roofing, Foundation and Home-Battery Installers
thesis: The residential solar tax credit died Dec 31, 2025 and dumped thousands of trained setters, closers and idle dialer seats onto the market; hire them cheap and run a pay-per-sat-appointment factory at $150-400 per sat appointment for hail-belt roofers, foundation repair, heat-pump/HVAC dealers and third-party-owned solar, at 40%+ margins.
who_pays: Roofing contractors (TX/OK/AR hail belt), foundation repair companies, HVAC and heat-pump dealers, and lease/PPA solar installers still eligible for the Section 48E commercial credit.
why_now: Solar installers slashed jobs and closed in Q1 2026 after the 25D credit expired, leaving experienced phone talent available at a discount; storm-season demand and PE-backed roofers paying per appointment create the buy side; installers pivoting to heat pumps and efficiency need net-new pipeline.

name: Nearshore Agent Staffing Reseller (Colombia/Mexico/Jamaica seats for US SMB call centers)
thesis: Bilingual nearshore agents cost roughly $8-12/hr loaded and bill $15-22/hr or $2,300-2,900 per seat per month, so a 50-seat book throws off $300K-600K/yr in gross margin and 200 seats is a $1M-2M+/yr business with no office and no dialer of your own.
who_pays: US insurance agencies, home-services companies, e-commerce support teams, medical practices, dealerships and other call centers that cannot staff reliably at US wages.
why_now: US contact-center labor is scarce while 2026 nearshore pricing spreads of $8-30/hr show buyers cannot price the market, leaving room for a trusted operator; Spanish-language demand and time-zone alignment favor LatAm over the Philippines; AI is taking simple calls and raising the premium on managed human seats for complex ones.

name: 2026 Midterm Political Dialing and P2P Texting Vendor for Down-Ballot Campaigns and PACs
thesis: The 2026 midterms are the most expensive non-presidential cycle ever ($10B-11.6B in media, $150M+ on texting alone) and phone banking bills $0.75-3.50 per completed contact, so a dialer-native shop selling paid phone banking, P2P texting, voter ID and GOTV to state legislative, county, judicial and PAC clients can clear $500K-2M in a four-month window.
who_pays: Campaigns, PACs and super PACs, state parties, ballot-measure committees, and political consultants who subcontract execution.
why_now: The Nov 3, 2026 general election makes Sept-Nov 2026 the peak spend window and the next one is 2028; five vendors control ~70% of texting spend, leaving thousands of down-ballot races underserved; political outreach is exempt from many commercial telemarketing rules but needs P2P and consent expertise most campaigns lack.

name: Medicare AEP and ACA OEP Seasonal Overflow Call Center with Built-In CMS Compliance
thesis: Every Oct 15-Dec 7 FMOs and Medicare agencies need surge capacity that already does CMS-compliant full-call recording with 10-year retention, TPMO disclaimers, scope-of-appointment capture and county-qualified transfers; a turnkey compliant desk bills $35-55/hr per agent or $40-120 per qualified transfer, runs $300K-1M in eight weeks, then flips the same seats to ACA open enrollment (Nov 1-Jan 15).
who_pays: FMOs, Medicare Advantage and Med Supp agencies, carriers' TPMO partners, and pay-per-call networks that need county-qualified transfers.
why_now: CY2027 Medicare marketing opens Oct 1, 2026 under a new CMS final rule that changes agent workflows, one-to-one consent is required for every TPMO data share, and non-compliant capacity gets contracts terminated, so buyers pay a premium for surge seats that are compliant on day one.

name: Membership Retention and Dues-Recovery Desk for Recurring-Membership Businesses
thesis: Membership businesses lose 15-30% of dues to silent churn, failed payments and unworked cancellation requests, so an outsourced save-and-recovery desk paid 15-25% of recovered dues plus a per-save bounty is found money for the client and scales across every recurring-revenue vertical from RV resort clubs to gyms to home-warranty plans.
who_pays: RV resort and campground membership networks, fitness chains, timeshare HOAs, home-warranty, pest-control, alarm and other subscription-service companies.
why_now: Card-decline rates and consumer belt-tightening are climbing in 2026, and 'click-to-cancel' enforcement is killing dark-pattern retention, which means saves must happen through real human conversations that most membership companies have no team to run.

name: Fractional Head of Contact Center / RevOps for PE-Backed Multi-Location Healthcare (DSOs, med spas, PT, vet)
thesis: PE-backed multi-location practices are centralizing scheduling and phones but cannot justify a $200K contact-center director per platform, so a fractional operator at $8K-15K/mo per platform running 3-5 platforms earns $300K-600K/yr plus equity kickers while designing the blended AI-plus-human phone stack they all need.
who_pays: PE-backed dental service organizations, med-spa and dermatology platforms, PT/ortho groups and veterinary roll-ups; the PE operating partner sponsors and pays.
why_now: Fractional VP-level RevOps already clears $10K-15K/mo in 2026, healthcare roll-ups face reimbursement pressure and must convert every inbound call, and AI phone agents are being sold into these platforms with no operator on the client side to make them work.

name: Lead Vendor Audit and Clawback Service (contingency-fee lead-quality forensics)
thesis: Call centers buying $50K-2M per month of leads routinely eat 10-30% junk (duplicates, dead numbers, missing consent artifacts, out-of-geo, litigator-list hits) and never file for credits, so an audit shop that scores every lead against consent, contactability and SLA and takes 25-35% of recovered dollars earns six figures per client per year with zero risk to the client.
who_pays: Insurance, home-services, roofing, debt-relief, education and Medicare call centers, sponsored by the CFO or VP of marketing who signs the lead invoices.
why_now: Consent standards are murky after the one-to-one rule was vacated, TrustedForm/Jornaya artifacts are inconsistently attached, and lead prices rose as buyers crowded into fewer verticals after solar collapsed, so margins now depend on clawing back junk that nobody has time to fight.

name: AI Voice Agent Implementation Partner for Trades and Dealership Service Departments with Human Overflow Desk
thesis: Build and operate after-hours, overflow and appointment-confirmation voice agents at $8K-20K setup plus $1.5K-5K/mo managed fee and a per-minute markup, backed by a small human fallback desk; 25 clients is $600K-1.2M/yr at software-like margins with a services wrapper competitors cannot copy.
who_pays: HVAC, plumbing and roofing companies, auto dealership service departments, med spas and property managers who miss thousands of dollars of calls a week.
why_now: Platform costs are $0.05-0.15/min self-serve but $0.25-0.33/min all-in and SMBs cannot wire Retell/Vapi to their CRM, dispatch board or calendar; certified-partner agencies with 500+ deployments prove the model, and every AI-voice failure story is creating demand for operators who also staff the human fallback.

name: Dialer Migration and Telecom Cost-Audit Practice (CCaaS implementation plus contingency carrier-bill recovery)
thesis: Every call center replatforms its dialer/CCaaS every 3-5 years and overpays carriers 10-25% on SIP trunks, DIDs and unused seats, so charge $15K-60K per migration (Convoso, Five9, Readymode, Genesys, HubSpot/GHL integrations), take 30-50% contingency on telecom savings found, and keep each client on a $2K-5K/mo admin retainer.
who_pays: 20-500 seat call centers, BPOs, insurance and Medicare agencies, and the dialer vendors themselves who pay implementation-partner and referral fees.
why_now: CCaaS vendors are shipping AI features in 2026 that force replatforming, contact centers are consolidating tools to cut costs, and vendor professional-services teams cannot keep up with migrations, so certified implementation partners are being courted with margin.

name: Ark-La-Tex Local Newsletter Network (Texarkana, then Shreveport, Tyler, Longview, Hot Springs)
thesis: A free daily 5-minute local email with ~18K subscribers sells ~$200K/yr of local advertising in a single small city (Naptown Scoop, Annapolis: ~$200K/yr from ~18K subs, 80%+ from ads — https://www.sidehustlenation.com/local-newsletter-business/), and 6AM City scaled the same playbook to $9.5M revenue, profitability by Q1 2026 and a 10–20% margin target (https://www.amediaoperator.com/news/6am-citys-secret-weapon-400-newsletters-with-no-staff/); with beehiiv plus AI drafting, one part-time editor per city and ~$2/subscriber paid acquisition (https://www.paved.com/blog/newsletter-acquisitions/), $50K funds 2–3 cities to ~15K subs each and a $400–600K/yr network within 24 months.
who_pays: Local advertisers — hospitals/clinics, med spas, realtors, car dealers, restaurants, festivals, law firms — buying primary header slots at $35–75 CPM and classified slots at $15–25 CPM, sold direct at 2–5x what ad networks pay (https://www.beehiiv.com/blog/newsletter-sponsorship-cost); secondary revenue from events, memberships and merch.
why_now: Medill's State of Local News 2025 counts 213 news-desert counties, 1,524 single-source counties and 136 outlets closed in the past year (https://localnewsinitiative.northwestern.edu/projects/state-of-local-news/2025/); local Facebook reach for businesses has collapsed and AI Overviews cut position-one organic CTR by 58% (Ahrefs, 300K keywords — https://www.medianama.com/2026/02/223-google-ai-overviews-click-through-rates-58-study/), so email is the last owned local channel; beehiiv paid-subscription revenue grew 138% in 2025 to $19M and is projected at $35M for 2026 (https://www.beehiiv.com/blog/the-state-of-paid-newsletters-2026). FIT 9/10: Joshua lives in Texarkana, sells ads/leads and manages reps for a living, and can automate the ops layer himself.

name: HubSpot / GoHighLevel / Convoso Tutorial Channel — B2B SaaS YouTube with recurring affiliate back end
thesis: B2B software tutorial content earns the highest RPM on YouTube — $15–45 per 1,000 views after YouTube's 45% cut, because enterprise-software advertisers pay $30–80 CPM (https://outlierkit.com/blog/highest-paying-youtube-niches) — and the tools themselves pay recurring referral commissions: GoHighLevel 40% recurring on $97–497/mo plans (https://openaffiliate.dev/programs/gohighlevel), HubSpot 30% recurring for a year via affiliate or 20% for three years as a Solutions Partner (https://www.hubspot.com/partner-commissions-faq), most AI/SaaS programs 20–40% recurring (https://outlierkit.com/resources/ai-tools-commission-rates/); a 2M-view/yr channel is ~$30–90K AdSense plus affiliate MRR plus implementation consulting, and evergreen finance/education-style channels sell for 30–36x monthly profit (https://flippa.com/blog/buy-youtube-channel/).
who_pays: Google AdSense (funded by B2B software advertisers), SaaS vendors' recurring affiliate/partner programs, and small businesses buying CRM/dialer setup and automation consulting off the back of the videos.
why_now: YouTube renamed 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content' on July 15, 2025 and in January 2026 terminated 16 AI-slop channels with 35M subscribers, 4.7B views and ~$10M/yr revenue (https://thenextweb.com/news/youtube-ai-slop-crackdown-faceless-creators-collateral-damage) while explicitly keeping human, insight-driven faceless content eligible (https://faceless.my/youtube/youtube-inauthentic-content-policy-faceless-ai-2026/) — screen-recorded 'here is how I actually built this in HubSpot' is exactly what survives, and the competition just got deleted. FIT 10/10: he runs these exact systems daily.

name: UGC + Whitelisting Creator Studio for DTC brands (manage 25 creators, sell the ad-account rights)
thesis: Brands pay $150–300 base per UGC video, $100–800 more for usage rights, and the real recurring money is whitelisting/Spark Ads at $500–2,000 per creator per month on top of production (https://ppc.io/blog/ugc-pricing; https://influee.co/blog/ugc-price); a studio that recruits and manages 25 creators, takes a 30–40% margin on ~8 videos each per month and keeps a share of whitelisting fees clears roughly $300–600K/yr (estimate: 25 x 8 x $250 x 35% ≈ $17.5K/mo production margin plus whitelisting), with near-zero capex.
who_pays: DTC and e-commerce brands' performance-marketing budgets; the IAB projects US creator advertising spend at $44B in 2026, up from $37B in 2025 (https://archive.com/blog/creator-economy-market-size), and brand sponsorship/influencer spend is the single largest creator-economy revenue category at $45–55B (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/creator-economy-statistics-2026-data-points).
why_now: Paid social needs constant creative refresh and AI video cannot supply a real person's ad account or trust; Meta paid nearly $3B to creators in 2025, ~60% for Reels, and is now paying $1K–3K/month to cross-post (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/18/meta-creator-pay-instagram-tiktok-youtube-facebook.html), so managed creators earn platform money on top of brand money. FIT 7/10: recruiting, scheduling and QA-scoring 25 creators is a call-center-floor problem, and he can build the creator-management app.

name: TikTok Shop Affiliate-Management Agency (outbound creator seeding for sellers)
thesis: eMarketer forecasts TikTok Shop US sales of $23.41B in 2026, up 48% YoY (https://www.dashboardly.io/statistics/tiktok-shop-affiliate-creator-statistics), affiliate creator content drives ~42% of that GMV (https://www.hamstergarage.com/article/tiktok-shop-affiliate-statistics-benchmarks-roi), and brands pay affiliate-management agencies $3,000–10,000/month retainers plus 5–15% of affiliate GMV or $80–200 per activated creator (https://thebrandbuddies.co/blog/tiktok-shop-agency-pricing/; https://marketerhire.com/blog/tiktok-shop-marketing-agency); eight seller clients at $5K = $480K/yr before GMV share. Side lane: run your own affiliate crew — average US commission is 13.02% and the top 1% of affiliates average $600K annual GMV (https://www.tkdami.com/blog/8216/; https://branvas.com/blogs/news/tiktok-shop-creator-earnings).
who_pays: TikTok Shop sellers and brands (retainer + % of affiliate GMV); TikTok itself pays creator commissions of 10–30% by category.
why_now: It is the fastest-growing US commerce channel and creator seeding is a pure outbound-volume game — thousands of sample requests, follow-ups and rep-style QA — which nobody in the creator world runs like a dialer floor. FIT 8/10: this is lead-gen ops with a different CRM; RV/outdoor gear is a natural first vertical.

name: Video-first podcast in a high-CPM vertical (insurance / finance / small-business ops), dual-monetized on YouTube and Spotify
thesis: Host-read mid-rolls pay $25–50 CPM for mid-tier shows and $60–120 for top-100 titles (https://www.millionpodcasts.com/blog/podcast-advertising-cost-cpm-rates-by-genre-size/), video podcasts earn ~24% higher CPM than audio-only (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/podcast-statistics-2026-advertising-data), and Spotify's Partner Program had hundreds of creators over $10K/month in its first month with top earners in six figures (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-02-13/spotifys-partner-program-helps-creators-increase-revenue-and-consumption-of-video-podcasts/), with podcasters like Chris Williamson reporting 2–3x more from Spotify than YouTube (https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/spotify-partner-program-podcasts-revenue-creators/); a vertical show (e.g., 'The Dialer Room' for call-center and sales-ops owners) stacks AdSense + Spotify + host-read sponsors + a services back end.
who_pays: Vertical advertisers buying host-reads, Spotify (Premium video engagement payouts plus 50% ad share), YouTube AdSense, and the show's own consulting/software upsells.
why_now: YouTube passed 1B monthly podcast viewers in Feb 2025 (https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/26/youtube-surpasses-1-billion-monthly-podcast-viewers/), Spotify video-podcast consumption nearly doubled after the Partner Program launched (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-01-08/spotify-partner-program-creator-success-stories/), and the IAB projects podcast ad revenue up another 9.6% in 2026 (https://www.airmeet.com/hub/blog/50-audio-podcast-and-video-podcast-statistics-for-2026/). FIT 7/10: he has a genuine operator niche (dialers, show rates, reps) most podcasters cannot fake.

name: Preschool Learning IP Studio built for streaming licensing and toys, not AdSense
thesis: Made-for-kids AdSense is close to dead — RPM ~$1–3, CPM often $0.25–0.35, and revenue drops >95% once a video is flagged made-for-kids (https://gyre.pro/blog/how-to-monetize-a-youtube-kids-channel) — so the 2026 money is licensing: Ms. Rachel's non-exclusive Netflix deal delivered 208M hours viewed in H1 2026 (https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/news/top-10-reports/youtube-creators-netflix-kids-2026-rankings/), Netflix followed with Blippi and Mark Rober (https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2025/08/20/netflix-is-all-in-on-childrens-programming-as-it-signs-deal-with-mark-rober-following-ms-rachel-success/), and Moonbug turned $120M of Cocomelon/Blippi purchases into a ~$3B sale (https://rollupeurope.com/p/moonbug-s-4-year-sprint-to-a-3b-exit-the-deal-that-fuelled-the-youtube-gold-rush); build a real-host character show with original songs, prove the audience on YouTube, then sell non-exclusive streaming licenses and consumer products. $50K funds a pilot season; a full slate realistically needs $150–300K (estimate based on production scope).
who_pays: Streamers (Netflix, Amazon Kids+) paying license fees for proven YouTube kids audiences; toy and edtech brand deals; consumer-products licensees; YouTube AdSense is a rounding error.
why_now: Streamers are actively buying digital-first kids IP because it comes with a built-in audience; kids' viewing has moved to YouTube on TVs; AI music, animation and editing tools cut per-episode cost dramatically, and Joshua already built a faceless-video content factory. FIT 6/10: needs an on-camera educator partner, but the factory, distribution and licensing ops are his.

name: AI-Training Footage Broker for small rights-holders (event videographers, drone pilots, churches, dashcams)
thesis: AI labs pay $1–4 per minute for unpublished, rights-clean video (https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/ai-giants-pay-thousands-for-creators-unused-footage-to-train-models/), marketplaces like Troveo have paid out $20M+ to 7,000+ rights holders (https://www.troveo.ai/resources/ai-training-data-statistics), but buyers want lots of 1,000+ hours per licensor (https://variety.com/vip/creators-are-licensing-content-to-train-ai-video-models-1236336720/) — so an aggregator that signs hundreds of small rights-holders and packages 10,000-hour thematic lots at $60–240 per hour with a 20–30% take earns $120K–$720K per lot (arithmetic on the cited per-minute rates); the same rights-ops machine can also sell voice clones into ElevenLabs' library, where creators have earned $22M (https://elevenlabs.io/blog/22-million-earned-by-voice-creators-on-elevenlabs).
who_pays: AI video-model developers (OpenAI, Google, Runway, etc.) via licensing marketplaces; the broker keeps a percentage and the rights-holder gets money for footage that was earning nothing.
why_now: 2025–26 is the first time raw footage has a wholesale price, and Cloudflare's Sept 15, 2026 default-block of training crawlers on ad-carrying pages makes licensed data scarcer and more valuable (https://www.forbes.com/sites/sandycarter/2026/07/01/cloudflare-moves-to-make-ai-pay-for-the-content-it-consumes/); TollBit publishers already earn hundreds to tens of thousands per month from AI access (https://mediacopilot.ai/ai-content-licensing-market-publishers-double-bind/). FIT 7/10: signing 500 videographers is an outbound-dialer job.

name: Founder & Executive LinkedIn Ghostwriting Shop (vertical-specialized)
thesis: Founders and executives pay $2,000–5,000/month for ghostwriting that produces pipeline (https://windmillgrowth.com/blogseo/linkedin-ghostwriter-cost), agency tiers run $2K–4K for 4–8 posts up to $8K–15K+/month (https://www.foundera.co/blog/linkedin-ghostwriting-pricing-guide-2026), and per-post rates are $150–800 (https://linkgenie.one/blog/how-much-does-a-linkedin-ghostwriter-cost); ten retainers at $3K = $360K/yr with zero capex, and B2B founders with $25K+ deal sizes report 10–20x ROI, which keeps churn low.
who_pays: B2B founders, executives, agency owners and franchise/dealer-group leaders (RV dealers, BPOs, SaaS) out of marketing budgets.
why_now: AI Overviews cut position-one organic CTR by 58% (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260518322756/en/New-Research-Googles-AI-Overviews-Now-Cost-Websites-58-of-Their-Clicks), pushing B2B demand-gen onto LinkedIn where a founder's face is the distribution; AI drafts the volume, but clients pay for interview-driven voice and strategy, which is the $4K+ tier. FIT 8/10: he already writes scripts and coaching copy for reps and knows two underserved verticals (RV/outdoor, call-center).

name: Corporate AI-Literacy Training for regional businesses (workshops + retainers)
thesis: Half-day team workshops bill $3,000–8,000 and full days $6,000–15,000 (https://bluecarrot.io/blog/corporate-training-rates/; https://tightslice.com/blog/ai-training-cost-2026), per-employee AI training runs $200–1,000 (https://www.pertamapartners.com/insights/cost-per-employee-ai-training-budgeting), and two workshops a week is $300–800K/yr; this is where 2026 'course' money actually is — B2C paid content converts at a 0.62% median free-to-paid rate (https://www.beehiiv.com/blog/the-state-of-paid-newsletters-2026) while businesses write five-figure checks for the same knowledge.
who_pays: SMB and mid-market owners, HR/L&D budgets, chambers of commerce, trade associations and dealer groups; small companies (100–999 employees) already spend $1,091 per employee on training (https://bluecarrot.io/blog/corporate-training-rates/).
why_now: Every company is being told to adopt AI and almost none have a practical operator to teach it; the credible trainer in 2026 is the non-engineer who actually ships with AI, not the consultant with slides. FIT 9/10: Joshua is the proof — he runs a department and ships apps solo with AI tools, and the call-center/RV-dealer world is an uncrowded first market.

name: Own-the-Audience Lead-Gen Channel in a high-LTV local vertical ('Moving to Texarkana / Ark-La-Tex' real estate first, Medicare second)
thesis: A tiny local real-estate YouTube channel (85K total views) produces 10–12 closings a year for a Killeen, TX agent (https://faribai.com/2026/09/19/you-dont-need-50000-subscribers-to-close-deals-on-youtube-heres-proof/); at the $429,300 May-2026 median price and the 2.82% average buyer-side commission (https://listwithclever.com/average-real-estate-commission-rate/) that is ~$12K per closing, ~$120–145K/yr, and the media owner can take a referral fee (25–35% is the customary range — estimate, industry convention) or license the channel to a brokerage instead of getting a license; run the same play for Medicare/insurance, where RPM alone is $15–32 (https://virlo.ai/blog/highest-rpm-niches-on-youtube) and a single customer is worth thousands in LTV.
who_pays: Brokerages and agents (referral fees or channel sponsorship), insurance agencies (per-lead or per-app), plus YouTube AdSense on top.
why_now: Relocation research now starts on YouTube, local news is gone (Medill 2025: https://localnewsinitiative.northwestern.edu/projects/state-of-local-news/2025/), and AI Overviews are gutting the web-lead sites agents used to buy from; first inbound lead lands at ~3 months and first closing at ~4 (https://www.jamilacademy.com/blog/youtube-for-real-estate-agents). FIT 8/10: he runs lead generation and show-rate optimization for a living, and Texarkana/Ark-La-Tex has no dominant relocation channel.

name: Owned-Catalog 24/7 Ambient Stream Network (lofi / sleep / nature / campfire) with Content ID
thesis: Lofi Girl is roughly a $3.5M/yr media business (https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/ai-music-gold-rush-how-lofi-girl-earns-%243-5-million/id1821580447?i=1000745078276); 24/7 streams earn on watch-hours rather than clicks — a 2026 study of 300 monetized channels put median RPM at ~$2.30 and YouTube measured 20%+ more ad revenue per hour with automatic mid-rolls (https://gyre.pro/blog/the-power-of-continuous-live-streams-boost-your-youtube-channels) — and owning the masters adds Content ID royalties, where a single track placed in a popular stream can generate thousands per year (https://www.waterandmusic.com/the-economics-of-24-7-lo-fi-hip-hop-youtube-livestreams/); commission real producers for work-for-hire masters, run 5–10 themed streams and license the catalog to other streamers.
who_pays: YouTube AdSense (hours x RPM), Content ID and DSP streaming royalties, and sleep/focus/outdoor sponsors buying the always-on placement.
why_now: TV-screen YouTube and sleep/focus listening are enormous and passive, and YouTube's inauthentic-content policy penalizes templated AI streams, so a human-made, owned catalog is the moat rather than the risk (https://faceless.my/youtube/youtube-inauthentic-content-policy-faceless-ai-2026/). FIT 8/10: his content-factory automation and RV/campfire aesthetic give him a differentiated theme.

name: Buy-and-Operate Media Assets: acquire cash-flowing newsletters and YouTube channels at 12–36x monthly profit
thesis: YouTube channels sell for 12–36x monthly profit — 1–3x annual — with faceless evergreen channels at the top and gaming/personality channels at the bottom (https://flippa.com/blog/buy-youtube-channel/), and real deals close below that (a faceless channel that hit $300K in 12 months sold for ~1.2x annual profit — https://flippa.com/blog/how-a-faceless-youtube-channel-sold-for-300k/); newsletters trade near acquisition cost per subscriber, ~$2/sub (https://www.paved.com/blog/newsletter-acquisitions/); $50K buys roughly $2–4K/month of existing profit, and the operator lifts it by selling sponsorships direct at 2–5x network CPM (https://www.beehiiv.com/blog/newsletter-sponsorship-cost) and adding a paid tier, then exits at a higher multiple.
who_pays: Sponsors, subscribers and platform payouts fund the acquired asset; a later buyer (Flippa/Empire Flippers) pays for the exit.
why_now: Amazon cut affiliate commissions by up to 50% for US publishers starting March 2026 (10% categories down to 4–5% — https://www.emarketer.com/content/amazon-cuts-affiliate-commissions-by-up-50--raising-pressure-on-publishers) while AI Overviews cut organic clicks 58%, creating distressed sellers of otherwise healthy audiences whose revenue can be re-based on sponsorship and subscriptions. FIT 7/10: an operator who can rebuild the monetization stack and automate the ops beats a passive buyer.

name: Texas Property-Tax Protest Firm (contingency, dialer-driven mass enrollment)
thesis: Texas local governments levied a record $125.05B in property taxes in 2024 (https://www.texaspolicyresearch.com/texas-property-tax-levies-1998-2025/); protest firms keep 25% (Ownwell) to 35-50% (traditional firms) of first-year savings with zero upfront fee (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/property-tax-protest-companies-cost), 60-80% of protests statewide win (https://propertytaxdesk.com/texas/property-tax-appeal-complete-guide/), and roughly 71% of DFW homeowners never filed in 2025 (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/protest-property-taxes-texas) - so a TDLR-licensed property-tax-consultant shop with an outbound dialer signs the non-filers and collects a slice of every reduction, every year, with no inventory and near-zero cost of goods.
who_pays: Homeowners and commercial/rental owners, out of realized tax savings (contingency; nothing if no reduction). Revenue estimate: 5,000 signed residential clients x 88% win rate x $774 average savings x 35% fee = ~$1.2M/yr (basis: Ownwell's 2025 88% success / $774 average-savings figures at https://www.ownwell.com/results/texas-property-tax-protest-results-agent-performance).
why_now: Texas levies rose another $2.7B in 2025 (https://texastaxpayers.com/texas-property-taxes-increased-2-7-billion-in-2025-whats-broken-and-how-do-we-actually-fix-it/), so the savings pool grows annually, and the fixed May 15 protest deadline (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/protest-property-taxes-texas) turns it into a predictable yearly outbound campaign. FIT: very high - this is a lead-gen + dialer + show-rate business, the exact machine Joshua runs by day.

name: IEEPA Tariff-Refund and Duty-Drawback Recovery Firm (contingency filings for small importers)
thesis: On Feb 20, 2026 the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that IEEPA never authorized tariffs, making every IEEPA duty paid from Feb 2025 through Feb 24, 2026 refundable (https://www.flexport.com/blog/the-supreme-courts-ieepa-tariff-ruling-next-steps-potential-refunds-and/); Penn Wharton projects up to $175B in refunds against $164.7B collected (https://budgetmodel.wharton.upenn.edu/p/2026-02-20-supreme-court-tariff-ruling/), and CBP's CAPE portal (launched Apr 20, 2026) lets 'importers of record and authorized brokers' file (Flexport). A recovery shop that files CAPE declarations, protests, and 99%-refund duty-drawback claims (https://gingercontrol.com/blog/duty-drawback-for-dummies) for small importers on contingency is skimming the largest tax refund in U.S. history - and ~80% of eligible drawback (~$15B/yr) already goes unclaimed (https://passportglobal.com/blog/recover-import-tariffs-duty-drawback-ecommerce/).
who_pays: Small and mid-size importers (e-commerce brands, distributors, RV/boat/parts dealers) out of refunded duties; CBP wires the refund by ACH into the importer's ACE account (Flexport). Contingency rate is not sourced - estimate 10-25% of recovery, basis: adjacent claims-recovery caps (Texas public adjusters 10%, Texas unclaimed-property finders 10%).
why_now: As of May 11, 2026 only 56,497 importers had enrolled for electronic refunds and $35.46B had been paid (Flexport) - a fraction of the $175B projected - so the long tail of small importers has not filed; protests carry a 180-day-from-liquidation deadline (Flexport), so this money is time-boxed through 2026-27. FIT: medium-high - pure outbound B2B prospecting to importers (Joshua's strength) paired with a licensed customs-broker partner for filings.

name: Medicare Advantage Telesales Agency (CMS fixed-commission book builder)
thesis: CMS sets the maximum broker payment at $694 per new Medicare Advantage enrollment plus $347/yr renewal for 2026, rising to $725/$363 in 2027, with PDP at $114/$57 (https://ritterim.com/blog/2027-maximum-broker-commissions-for-medicare-advantage-and-medicare-part-d/) - paid by carriers, never by the senior - so a compliant licensed agency running 10 agents at 40 applications/month builds a renewal annuity. Estimate: 4,800 enrollments/yr x $694 = ~$3.3M first-year commissions plus ~$1.67M/yr in renewals per retained cohort (basis: CMS 2026 rates above; agent productivity assumed).
who_pays: Medicare Advantage and Part D carriers (UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Aetna, etc.) via CMS-capped commissions; the beneficiary pays nothing.
why_now: Peak 65: a record 4.18M Americans turned 65 in 2025 (11,400/day) (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/the-us-has-reached-the-peak-of-peak-65-its-time-to-apply-retirement-readiness-lessons-from-the-boomer-experience-302360086.html) and ~4.1M more turn 65 in 2026 with the surge running through 2027 (https://natlawreview.com/press-releases/4-million-americans-turn-65-2026-ltc-news-expands-free-tools-aging-and-long); CMS raised max compensation for 2026 and again for 2027 (Ritter). FIT: very high - licensed telesales with dialers, scripts, and QA is Joshua's core competency; TCPA/CMS marketing rules are the moat.

name: Texas Public-Adjusting Firm for Hail and Severe-Storm Claims
thesis: Texas caps public-adjuster fees at 10% of the settlement under Tex. Ins. Code 4102.104 (https://insuranceclaimrecoverysupport.com/public-adjuster-in-texas/), and U.S. severe convective storms produced $51B in insured losses in 2025 - the third straight year above $50B, more than any other natural-disaster category (https://www.iii.org/press-release/triple-i-severe-convective-storms-generate-more-than-50b-in-insured-losses-for-third-consecutive-year-041326). A TDI-licensed PA who signs 100 underpaid roof/commercial claims a year at a $40K average settlement uplift collects ~$400K (estimate: 100 x $40K x 10%; uplift assumed). Start as a licensed adjuster at an existing firm, then own the shop.
who_pays: Property owners, out of the insurance settlement; ultimately the insurer's claim payment. Fee is calculated on net recoverable amount after deductible (https://www.tigeradjusters.com/blog/how-much-do-public-adjusters-charge).
why_now: Texas leads the nation in raw hail exposure and insurers are under acute pressure (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/news/severe-convective-storms/); Gallagher Re puts total 2025 economic SCS damages above $68B (Triple-I release above). Rising deductibles and depreciation holdbacks mean more underpaid claims to reopen. FIT: high - claims are sold by phone/door after every storm, and a call center can run intake for a licensed PA.

name: Unclaimed-Property Finder / Asset-Recovery Firm (Texas 10%-cap model)
thesis: Texas is holding nearly $11B in unclaimed property (https://www.kbtx.com/2026/03/23/texas-has-nearly-11b-unclaimed-property-about-487m-is-linked-bryan-college-station/) and returned more than $450M in FY2025 (https://www.recordinglaw.com/us-laws/unclaimed-property/texas-unclaimed-property/); state law lets finders charge up to 10% under Tex. Prop. Code 74.507 once property has been reported 24+ months (https://heirclaim.com/unclaimed-money/texas; https://www.claimittexas.gov/app/faq-ucp). A skip-tracing shop that targets only business-owner, estate, and dissolved-entity claims worth $10K+ earns $1K+ per file with no inventory, and can replicate across states with similar caps.
who_pays: Claimants (businesses, heirs, individuals) from the recovered funds; the Texas Comptroller pays the claim. Revenue estimate: 100 signed claims/month x $15K average x 10% = $150K/month (basis: fee cap above; claim size assumed - no public distribution of claim sizes was found).
why_now: The pile keeps growing ($422M returned FY2024 -> $450M+ FY2025 per https://comptroller.texas.gov/about/media-center/news/20240905-texas-comptroller-glenn-hegar-announces-record-422-million-in-unclaimed-property-returned-in-fiscal-2024-1725464185918), while AI skip-tracing and data automation collapse the cost of locating owners. FIT: very high - locating owners is data work Joshua can automate; converting them is a phone job his reps already do.

name: DOT Compliance C/TPA for Micro-Fleets (drug consortium + Clearinghouse + audit-readiness subscription)
thesis: About 580,000 active carriers are registered with FMCSA and 91.5% run 10 or fewer trucks (https://maxdispatchservice.com/how-many-trucking-companies-in-the-us/; https://www.freightwaves.com/news/there-are-292000-shippers-in-america-and-97-of-carriers-have-10-trucks-or-less-the-match-has-been-right-in-front-of-you-the-whole-time), and every one of them is legally required to be in a random drug/alcohol testing program, run Clearinghouse queries, and keep driver-qualification files; consortium enrollment runs $50-$150 per driver per year plus $40-$80 per test (https://www.foley.io/dot-drug-testing-consortium). Bundle consortium, Clearinghouse queries, DQ files, and mock-audit prep at ~$400/yr per micro-fleet and 2,000 clients is ~$800K of mandated recurring revenue (estimate; pricing assumed from the Foley ranges).
who_pays: Small carriers and owner-operators, compelled by 49 CFR Part 382 and FMCSA audits; non-compliance means out-of-service orders and fines.
why_now: 2026 is FMCSA's biggest rule year in a decade: English-proficiency violations are now out-of-service conditions (https://heavyvehicleinspection.com/blog/post/new-fmcsa-rules-2026-fleet-guide), and the Feb 2026 non-domiciled CDL final rule took effect Mar 16, 2026 (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/02/13/2026-02965/restoring-integrity-to-the-issuance-of-non-domiciled-commercial-drivers-licenses-cdl) with an estimated 194,000 drivers affected (https://enotrans.org/article/legal-back-and-forth-continues-for-cdls/) - small fleets are scrambling and paying for help. Texarkana sits on the I-30 freight corridor. FIT: high - subscription ops + outbound sales to a captive, mandated buyer; a micro-SaaS portal is a natural build.

name: Court-Mandated Ignition-Interlock Service Center (multi-county TX/AR)
thesis: Texas judges must order interlocks for repeat DWI offenders and commonly do for first offenses at 0.15+ BAC, with installation due within 30 days of conviction (https://www.intoxalock.com/state-requirements/texas; https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/ignition-interlock-device); devices lease for $60-$90/month plus $70-$150 to install (https://www.intoxalock.com/knowledge-center/budget-for-the-cost-of-an-ignition-interlock; https://www.interlock.com/costs-pricing/costs-of-an-ignition-interlock-device). An authorized multi-brand service center with 400 devices on the road grosses ~$30K/month (estimate: 400 x $75) from customers the court sends you, in a North American market of $668.9M in 2025 (https://www.persistencemarketresearch.com/market-research/north-america-ignition-interlock-devices-market.asp).
who_pays: DWI defendants, out of pocket, monthly, as a condition of driving imposed by the court/DPS.
why_now: Texas DPS logged 20,781 (Q1), 22,023 (Q3) and 21,812 (Q4) DWI arrests in 2024 (https://www.dps.texas.gov/sites/default/files/documents/administration/crime_records/docs/dwireport/dwirecidivism2024q1.pdf; https://www.dps.texas.gov/sites/default/files/documents/administration/crime_records/docs/dwireport/dwirecidivism2024q3.pdf; https://www.dps.texas.gov/sites/default/files/documents/administration/crime_records/docs/dwireport/dwirecidivism2024q4.pdf) - roughly 85,000+ per year annualized (estimate from three reported quarters; no statewide install count was found). Rural counties around Texarkana have long drive times to the nearest service center. FIT: medium - a physical bay and installer are needed; Joshua's edge is referral marketing to DWI attorneys, probation offices, and courts.

name: ADAS Calibration Center (insurance-paid sublet work for body and glass shops)
thesis: 28.3% of collision repairs now require ADAS calibration per Q4 2025 CCC data (https://pennypincher.com/articles/insurance/auto/adas-repair-costs-insurance-windshield-calibration) at $300-$600 per calibration (https://www.caliber.com/services/auto-glass/auto-glass-calibration/how-much-does-adas-calibration-cost), paid by insurers under comprehensive/collision coverage (https://blog.glass.net/glass-quotes/adas-calibration-insurance-coverage/); a standalone calibration bay doing 8 jobs/day at $400 grosses ~$800K/yr (estimate) in a North American market of $1.3B in 2025 growing to $2.5B by 2033 (https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/adas-calibration-services-market-115495). Capital: likely $75K-$150K for targets, scan tools, and a level bay (estimate; no sourced figure found), so above the $50K default.
who_pays: Auto insurers (through body shops and glass shops that sublet the calibration), OEM warranty, and fleets; the consumer pays at most a deductible.
why_now: Windshield replacements now routinely exceed $1,500 because of calibration (pennypincher link above), and small-town body/glass shops cannot justify the equipment, so they sublet. The global market is valued at $5.24B in 2025 rising to $12.85B by 2034 (Fortune Business Insights). FIT: medium - requires a technician and shop; Joshua's edge is B2B sales to every body/glass shop in the Ark-La-Tex plus ops dashboards.

name: Cost-Segregation Study Firm riding permanent 100% bonus depreciation
thesis: The One Big Beautiful Bill (P.L. 119-21) made 100% bonus depreciation permanent for property placed in service after Jan 19, 2025 and created 100% expensing for Qualified Production Property, both of which require a cost-segregation study as the substantiating document (https://www.cbh.com/insights/articles/trumps-tax-bill-bonus-depreciation-cost-segregation/); studies bill $5K-$15K for commercial buildings, about $10K per $1M property, and owners typically get a 4x-10x first-year return on the fee (https://www.recostseg.com/post/cost-seg-pricing-5k-vs-15k; https://corporatetaxadvisors.com/cost-of-cost-segregation-study-complete-pricing-guide-for-2026/). A firm with one engineer plus a CPA-referral sales channel doing 150 studies/yr is ~$1.5M in revenue (estimate).
who_pays: Commercial property owners, apartment and short-term-rental investors, and manufacturers, referred by their CPAs; the fee is paid out of first-year tax savings.
why_now: Permanence removed the phase-down that would have hit zero by 2027 (Cherry Bekaert link above), so every 2025-2026 acquisition and every new manufacturing facility (QPP construction must begin before Jan 1, 2029) needs a study now. FIT: medium-high - outbound prospecting to CPAs and investors plus a software front end for intake; engineering can be subcontracted.

name: Fire and Life-Safety Inspection Company (code-mandated recurring ITM routes)
thesis: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157 and NFPA standards require every commercial building to have extinguishers, sprinklers, and alarms inspected on fixed schedules, which is why the fire-protection testing, inspection, and certification market was $1B in 2025 and heads to $1.27B by 2030 with maintenance services the largest recurring segment (https://www.researchandmarkets.com/report/fire-protection-system-testing-inspection-and-certification); a route-based inspection company sells 12-month contracts that renew forever, and every deficiency found converts into repair revenue.
who_pays: Building owners, property managers, and commercial tenants, compelled by the fire marshal, the building code, and their insurer; failure means citations, occupancy risk, and coverage problems.
why_now: The market is growing 4.6%-5.4% a year on regulatory and insurance mandates (ResearchAndMarkets above; https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/fire-protection-system-market-104820), and insurers are tightening commercial requirements after three straight years of $50B+ storm losses (https://www.iii.org/press-release/triple-i-severe-convective-storms-generate-more-than-50b-in-insured-losses-for-third-consecutive-year-041326). FIT: medium - needs a licensed technician; Joshua's edge is route-density selling, scheduling, and an inspection-reporting app.

name: TEFA-Approved Education Vendor (microschool, tutoring, and therapy network)
thesis: Texas launched a $1B Education Freedom Account program for 2026-27 paying up to $10,474 per private-school student, up to $30,000 for students with disabilities, and $2,000 per homeschooler (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/texas-opens-applications-for-texas-education-freedom-accounts; https://thetexan.news/issues/education/almost-100-000-students-set-to-receive-texas-education-freedom-account-funds-in-next-school/article_eeb07b7a-2068-4cbf-bea3-66d292f52d67.html); 200,003 students applied (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-celebrates-record-breaking-school-choice-demand) and families can only spend the money with Comptroller-approved vendors - tutors, therapists, curriculum, microschools - who apply on a rolling basis through the Odyssey portal with 4-6 week approval (https://educationfreedom.texas.gov/providers-vendors/; https://getesapaid.com/tefa-vendors). An accredited microschool or a tutoring/therapy network in Texarkana captures state money that must be spent inside the marketplace.
who_pays: The State of Texas (Comptroller, disbursed via Odyssey/Stripe) from each family's ESA balance; the family bears no cost.
why_now: The Comptroller is asking to double the program to more than $2B for 2027-29 (https://www.ksstradio.com/2026/09/texas-comptroller-seeks-to-double-school-choice-budget-to-over-2-billion/) and private schools are already reporting rapid growth (https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/texas-education-freedom-accounts-private-school-growth-8-11-2026/); the vendor database is young and under-supplied outside the big metros. FIT: medium-high - Joshua's edge is enrollment marketing and a vendor-side app; the teaching/therapy itself is hired.

name: Rural Health Transformation Program Implementation Vendor / Grant-Compliance Consultant
thesis: OBBBA created a $50B Rural Health Transformation Program paying $10B a year from FY2026-2030, and Texas won the largest first-year award at $281.3M for its 'Rural Texas Strong' plan covering AI/telehealth, workforce, and infrastructure (https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/02/cms-launches-50b-rural-health-transformation-program; https://www.rhtpnavigator.com/states/texas; https://pfd.hhs.texas.gov/rural-health-transformation-program); the state and its rural hospitals and clinics must spend that money through procured vendors and document it to federal audit standards, so a firm that builds the telehealth workflows, dashboards, and data pipelines, or manages sub-grant compliance for rural providers, bills against money that is legally required to be spent by 2030. Fee basis: no RHTP consultant schedule was found; the analogous FEMA grant-management allowance is 5-7% of award (https://www.fema.gov/appeal/grant-management-costs), which on Texas's $281M is a $14M-$20M annual services pool.
who_pays: Texas HHSC and sub-awardee rural hospitals, FQHCs, and clinics, using CMS federal funds.
why_now: Awards were announced for FY2026 with first-year state awards averaging $200M (Morgan Lewis above), and Texas HHSC is running procurements now while refusing pre-procurement vendor meetings (https://pfd.hhs.texas.gov/rural-health-transformation-program) - the RFPs are the only door, and they are open. Texarkana anchors a rural Ark-La-Tex hospital region. FIT: high - Joshua ships ops dashboards and healthcare-adjacent call-center workflows; a job path (grant/program manager at an RHTP consultancy or rural hospital) is also open immediately.
